The doctor who performed the autopsy on 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez is set to give the difficult details of her death Friday at a hearing to determine whether singer D4vd, whose legal name is David Burke, should go on trial in her killing.

The April autopsy report from Dr. Grant Ho of the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner found that Rivas Hernandez's death was a homicide caused by penetrating wounds to her upper body.

The dismembered and decomposing body was discovered in a Tesla towed from the Hollywood Hills in September, 4 1/2 months after the time authorities say Rivas Hernandez was killed.

That meant the autopsy was limited by “extensive postmortem changes.” The body had so degraded that examiners couldn’t even determine the girl's eye color.

Prosecutors are seeking to prove Burke began sexually abusing Rivas Hernandez when she was 13 and he was 18, then stabbed her to death when she threatened to reveal their long sexual history and crater his career. They allege he dismembered the body in his garage, and a police analyst testified in the preliminary hearing that samples pulled from apparent blood stains there matched the DNA of Rivas Hernandez.

Burke has pleaded not guilty to murder, sexual abuse of a child and mutilation of a body, and his lawyers have said he is innocent.

There is some uncertain language in the autopsy report, which says the wounds “may represent sharp force injuries.” The defense, which has been seeking to dismantle the forensic evidence, may seize on this.

One wound on the upper abdomen penetrated the liver, the report said. Another, on the left chest, damaged her ribs. A tube top she was wearing appeared to be cut in three places.

Toxicology tests on Rivas Hernandez's liver showed a low level of alcohol, but it may have been produced postmortem by bacteria and didn’t appear to be a factor in her death, the report said.

LA County’s Chief Medical Examiner Dr. Odey C. Ukpo gave a statement with the autopsy report objecting to police keeping his office from releasing the results for several months, calling it “unfathomable” that her grieving family would have to wait so long to find out what had happened to her.

In an interview with The Associated Press in June, Ukpo elaborated, saying keeping information sealed “goes completely against our mission.”

“It’s so important for us to release the information that she did not die from something natural, she did not die from drugs, she was stabbed,” Ukpo said. “And then we start to look back at what made her vulnerable to be in that situation.”

An indie-pop singer whose music and online presence brought him a huge following, D4vd's songs and videos often have dark and violent imagery often delivered through an alter-ego character he calls Itami. His breakthrough single in 2022 was called “Romantic Homicide,” one of several of his songs with more than a billion plays on Spotify.

As officials review widely circulated bystander videos of the fatal police shooting of a homeless man in Madison, Wisconsin, one key perspective won’t be emerging: footage from the officers’ body-worn cameras.

Unlike nearly every other similarly sized city, Madison doesn’t require its police to wear them.

The absence of that footage has left residents in the dark about key moments leading up to the shooting, when police say Corey Ruiz pulled a knife during a struggle with four officers, injuring one of them. That officer then fired the shots, according to police. All four officers have been placed on administrative leave pending a state investigation.

In the meantime, the deadly encounter has reignited a contentious debate about body cameras, one that has long vexed local officials and pitted some of the city’s progressive groups against each other.

This past November, the Madison Common Council rejected a proposal to redirect funding from a police oversight group to a body-camera program. A new proposal to allocate $414,800 for a three-year roll out of the program is expected to be approved by the legislative body.

Police Chief John Patterson has described the proposal as “modest,” adding that the cameras had become “essential tools for the modern police officer.”

Law enforcement experts tend to agree and some expressed surprise that the city’s nearly 500 officers weren’t already using the cameras.

“There are very, very few agencies of that size that do not have a body-worn camera program,” said Michael D. White, a criminal justice professor at Arizona State University who led training on camera adoption for the U.S. Department of Justice.

“Madison has a long-standing tradition of being an innovative, progressive police department, so it’s startling,” he added.

As far back as 2016, roughly 80% of police departments with 500 or more sworn officers had acquired body-cameras — a figure that White said was now approaching 100%.

Over the last decade, Madison officials have repeatedly debated adopting the cameras. Committees have borne subcommittees, which have produced feasibility studies, amendments and hours of debate.

Local officials primarily blame budget concerns, along with political inertia, for the ongoing stalemate. Another common source of opposition, identified in a 2021 feasibility study, came from community groups worried the cameras would be used to surveil and criminalize marginalized groups.

“I cannot approve something that doesn’t have a policy and procedure behind it that is potentially going to hinder the community more than help the community,” said Veronica Figueroa, then a member of the body-worn camera subcommittee.

As camera adoption has become more widespread in recent years, those concerns have largely faded away, according to Common Council President Sabrina Madison.

But she said local officials have largely been preoccupied by another issue: finding shelter for a homeless population that has grown since the COVID-19 pandemic.

“It was like: if we’re going to figure out anything, we’re going to figure out how to fund shelter operations,” Madison told The Associated Press on Thursday. “So the last couple years, that’s where the focus has been.”

The city did briefly conduct a body camera pilot program in the summer of 2024. A subsequent report found the cameras had little impact on officers’ behavior or the community’s feeling toward police.

Dr. Broderick Turner, an independent researcher who analyzed the program and authored the report, noted the length of the pilot — only 90 days — meant there was little time for anyone to notice a meaningful difference. And he described demographic differences in the city's response.

“Black communities tend to want body cameras, but Madison is majority white,” Turner said. “The groups opposed were less impacted by crime and less impacted by policing.”

For some in the city, Wednesday’s shooting has surfaced memories of Tony Robinson, an unarmed 19-year-old who was fatally shot by Madison police in 2015.

His death ultimately led to the creation of the Office of the Independent Police Monitor.

This past winter, Madison lawmakers shot down a budget proposal that would have paid for a body camera program by cutting funds to the monitor.

Katey Nelson, a member of the police civilian oversight board, said the amendment had presented residents with a “false choice.”

“There are cuts that can be made with the Madison Police Department or the County Sheriff’s department, but they’re trying to pit similar agendas against each other,” she said.

“Nobody can agree on anything,” Nelson added. “Now we’re here, looking at another police shooting where we don’t have what we need to make sure the officers are held accountable.”

Officials are gathering Friday in Ontario to take delight in a new U.S.-Canada bridge over the Detroit River, an international span that is expected to enhance trade on both sides of the border and give travelers another route to both countries.

A ceremony is taking place in Windsor, Ontario, before the Gordie Howe International Bridge opens to traffic Monday. It was supposed to be a celebration on the bridge deck with officials from both countries, but Canada said no to a joint gathering after President Donald Trump this week suddenly announced 50% tariffs on Canadian goods entering the U.S.

“It's regretful that we're at this point in time with our trade relationship. We're hopeful for better days ahead,” Windsor Mayor Drew Dilkens told WXYZ-TV in Detroit.

More than 70% of Canada’s exports go to the U.S., making America its largest trade partner, and Detroit is the No. 1 port for truck traffic on the U.S.-Canada border, according to the U.S. Department of Transportation.

The Howe bridge will instantly create competition. For nearly a century, the privately owned Ambassador Bridge has been the only route for large commercial trucks moving between the U.S. and Canada at Detroit.

Detroit Mayor Mary Sheffield said she had been invited to a two-country event Friday before things abruptly changed.

“It will be vital for our economy,” Sheffield said of the bridge, sidestepping a question about whether it had become a “political football” in the rocky relationship between the countries.

The bridge is named for Howe, a famous Canadian who played hockey for the NHL's Detroit Red Wings. He died in 2016. Construction, which began in 2018, took years, partly because of a global slowdown caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.

The six-lane bridge is 1.5 miles (2.4 kilometers) long and stands 151 feet (46 meters) above the Detroit River at its highest point. Pedestrians and bicyclists carrying proper identification will be able to cross it for free in a few weeks.

Canada paid to build the bridge at an estimated cost of $6.4 billion. A recent agreement says Canada will share some toll revenue with the U.S. government for 15 years. Michigan will also get a share, but not until Canada’s costs are recovered, likely decades in the future.

A teenager accused of killing four people nearly two years ago at Apalachee High School in Georgia is due in court Friday for a plea and sentencing hearing.

Colt Gray, 16, previously pleaded not guilty to murder and other charges in the Sept. 4, 2024, shooting that killed two students and two teachers, and left several others wounded, at the high school about 45 miles (73 kilometers) northeast of Atlanta.

Barrow County Superior Court Judge Nicholas Primm has set a “Non-Negotiated Plea and Sentencing Hearing” to begin Friday. Gray's trial had been scheduled to start in mid-October in Columbia County, about 100 miles (160 kilometers) from where the shooting happened, after the judge agreed to a defense request for a change of venue.

A jury in March convicted Gray's father, Colin Gray, on charges including second-degree murder and involuntary manslaughter, and he is scheduled to be sentenced next week. Prosecutors said the elder Gray gave his son the assault-style rifle used to open fire at the school.

Teachers Richard “Ricky” Aspinwall, 39, and Cristina Irimie, 53, and students Mason Schermerhorn and Christian Angulo, both 14, died in the shooting. Another teacher and eight more students were wounded, seven of them hit by gunfire.

A non-negotiated plea means that the state and the defense have not reached an agreement on a sentence. Unlike a negotiated plea deal, in which a defendant often pleads guilty in exchange for an agreed-upon sentence and possibly reduced charges, sentencing is left entirely to the judge. The judge decides the sentence after hearing each side’s summary of the case, evidence and sentencing recommendation.

Prosecutors have indicated in court filings that they intend to call teenage victims and witnesses to testify and to show surveillance video and crime scene photos during Friday's hearing. They have also noted that they may introduce a slew of records, including 911 calls and Colt Gray's school, medical and social media records.

Gray's defense attorney wrote in a court filing that he plans to call a psychologist, someone who works at the juvenile detention center where he has been held and his grandmother to testify.

Gray, who was 14 at the time of the shooting, was charged as an adult with 55 total counts, including murder in the four deaths and 25 counts of aggravated assault.

Investigators testified that the teenager carried the rifle onto the school bus with the barrel wrapped in a poster board. They said he left his second-period class and emerged from a bathroom with the rifle, shooting people in a classroom and hallway.

Investigators have said Colt Gray carefully plotted the shooting at the high school of 1,900 students. A Georgia Bureau of Investigation agent testified that the teen left a notebook in his classroom with step-by-step instructions and a diagram to prepare for the assault, including an estimate that he could kill as many as 26 people and wound as many as 13 others.

Sheriff’s deputies interviewed Colt and Colin Gray in May 2023 about an online threat linked to the son. Colt Gray denied making the threat. He skipped eighth grade, enrolled as a freshman at Apalachee after the academic year had begun and then had a spotty attendance record.

Investigators found a shrine in Colt Gray's bedroom to Nikolas Cruz, the shooter in the 2018 massacre at Florida’s Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School, prosecutors said.

An investigator testified during Colin Gray's trial that he had been aware that his son's mental health had deteriorated and sought help from a counseling service weeks before the shooting, citing anger, anxiety and volatility. But the father never followed through on getting help for his son, the investigator said.

His mother, Marcee Gray, who was separated from Colin Gray, told investigators she had urged him weeks before the shooting to secure his guns and restrict their son’s access to them. Instead, over time, Colin Gray bought the boy ammunition, a gun sight and other shooting accessories, records show.

News.title: Ebola death toll passes 1,000 as outbreak shows no signs of slowing
News.content:
More than 1,000 people have now died in the outbreak of Ebola in the Congo, as medics struggle to curb the fastest-growing epidemic of the virus.

Dozens of deaths are being recorded each day and modelling has forecast that, in a worst case scenario, it could become the worst Ebola outbreak in history.

The outbreak, centred on the north east of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), passed the four-figure death milestone little more than two months after it was first declared.

By contrast, the worst outbreak of the haemorrhagic fever on record, which struck West Africa from 2014 to 2016, took eight months from the first case to reach 1,000 deaths. It went on to kill 11,000 people.

The latest figures from the DRC’s national public health institute show 2,536 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,033 deaths, with at least 738 patients in isolation or hospitalised.

News.title: Inflation fall a ‘false dawn’, Burnham warned
News.content:
Falling inflation is a “false dawn” for Andy Burnham, economists warned after the pace of price rises slowed in June.

The consumer prices index (CPI) fell from 2.8pc in May to 2.6pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), beating economists’ expectations of a drop to 2.7pc to mark the lowest rate in 15 months.

Lower petrol and diesel prices drove the slowdown amid a short-lived peace deal between the US and Iran, while price pressures from chocolate, oils and fats, dairy and meat also weakened.

However, economists warned a rise in household energy bills in July may already have pushed inflation back up above 3pc.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants, said: “June’s slowdown is a false dawn as it may have already been reversed this month with higher energy bills, following Ofgem’s energy price cap rise, likely to have lifted inflation above 3pc.”

July’s 13pc increase in the energy price cap has pushed typical annual bills to around £1,862, while renewed fighting between the US and Iran has reignited concerns over oil and gas supplies.

Mr Thiru said elevated inflation would create a fresh headache for John Healey, the newly appointed Chancellor, by squeezing household budgets, raising government borrowing costs and limiting his room for tax cuts or spending increases.

Charlotte O’Leary, at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “June’s peace deal and the subsequent reduction in oil and gas prices helped cool consumer price inflation. This will be a welcome figure to start the new Prime Minister’s premiership, but the honeymoon period will be short-lived.”

The Bank of England will also be watching closely as it weighs further interest rate cuts, though economists warned renewed instability in the Middle East and higher energy bills could keep inflation close to 3pc for the rest of the year.

Mr Healey said: “Falling inflation is news families want to hear, but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need.”

News.title: Russia destroys Ukraine HIV warehouse
News.content:
A Russian missile strike has destroyed $2.6m (£1.9m) worth of HIV prevention supplies in Ukraine, according to an international aid group.

The Alliance for Public Health said the attack on Sunday night near Kyiv hit a warehouse holding 62 million prevention items earmarked for Ukraine’s harm reduction programmes next year. It includes syringes, needles, alcohol wipes, and condoms intended to support more than 300,000 people.

“This is not just another strike. It is an attack on 300,000 Ukrainians who depend on HIV prevention services and on their fundamental right to health,” said Andriy Klepikov, executive director of the Alliance for Public Health.

Efforts to prevent the spread of HIV rely heavily on harm reduction programmes that supply sterile syringes and needles to people who inject drugs, alongside condoms and other supplies that help curb sexual transmission.

Mr Klepikov said the destruction of the warehouse would not immediately disrupt services, because his organisation had moved its supplies for the rest of the year out of central storage and into regional distribution centres several weeks ago as part of contingency planning.

“Russia failed,” he said, adding that the Alliance had notified international partners and appealed for urgent support to rebuild next year’s inventory.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

Sports.title: Real Madrid willing to sell Aurelien Tchouameni to Man Utd in £68m deal in order to fund ambitious Rodri transfer
Sports.content:
JOSE MOURINHO is ready to sell Aurelien Tchouameni to Manchester United so Real Madrid can fund a swoop for World Cup winner Rodri.

The Red Devils have enquired about £68million-rated Tchouameni, 26, with boss Michael Carrick keen on a specialist defensive midfielder to join new boys Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.



Real are desperate to sign Manchester City ace Rodri, who was named the World Cup’s best player after leading Spain to glory over Argentina on Sunday.

The La Roja captain, 30 — valued at £85m — has 12 months left on his Etihad deal and will miss the start of the Prem season as he needs minor back surgery.



New Real coach Jose had planned on keeping France star Tchouameni, who is under contract until 2028 and had verbally agreed a new deal at the Bernabeu.

But SunSport understands the 15-time European Cup winners are prepared to cash in.

Tchouameni joined Real from Monaco for an initial fee of £68m in 2022.

Real sources say United’s interest in the player is “strong” now the World Cup has finished.

The Red Devils have lost two midfielders with Brazil veteran Casemiro, 34, now at Inter Miami, while 25-year-old Uruguayan Manuel Ugarte sustained a serious knee injury at the tournament.

Tchouameni’s age, availability and pedigree, having started the 2022 World Cup final against the Argies and won the Champions League with Real, appeals to United.

The former Monaco star also fits their preferred age range of 22-26.



United had the chance to sign Tchouameni from Monaco in 2021.

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, the Old Trafford gaffer at the time, wanted to bring in a midfielder and was keen on Declan Rice, who was then at West Ham.

But the club had not budgeted for a player in that position.



Madrid bought Tchouameni to replace Casemiro after United bought him in a £70m deal in 2022.

The Red Devils have had mixed success with signings from Madrid.

Casemiro impressed in his first and last seasons but was released last month, while injury-prone Raphael Varane arrived aged 28 in 2021 and was also let go two years ago.

And Angel Di Maria was a £59.7m British-record buy in 2014 — but he lasted less than a year.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola ‘makes decision’ on Italy job with Man City legend ‘demanding £17MILLION-a-year salary’
Sports.content:
PEP GUARDIOLA is reportedly ready to snub the chance to become Italy’s new boss.

The six-time Premier League title winner, 55, has been assessing his options after quitting Manchester City at the end of last season.



And Guardiola held talks with Italy’s technical director Paolo Maldini over moving into international management for the first time.

But the former Barcelona and Bayern Munich chief appears to have made a decision on his future.



Gazzetta dello Sport report Guardiola is set to reject Italy’s advances after failing to agree personal terms.

The Spaniard is demanding a deal which would see him pocket an eye-watering £17MILLION-a-year.



But the Italian FA, who have been prepared to break the bank in order to land their top target, have only offered £8.5m-per-year.

Maldini, 58, admitted to having “little optimism” about tempting Guardiola after their discussions.

Italian FA president Giovanni Malago also conceded they were facing an uphill battle to get the deal over the line.

He said: “Financial exceptions have been made, exceptions that for example may concern the name that is so overbearing in these hours: Pep Guardiola.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“Exceptions that I am not here to explain, for obvious reasons. But it is not certain that this thing will go through.”

Man City legend Guardiola bagged 20 trophies during a glittering decade-long spell in the Etihad Stadium dugout.

And Italy were hoping to persuade him to make a quickfire return to management after they missed out on World Cup qualification.

Roberto Mancini and Andrea Pirlo are also in the running to take charge of the Azzurri.



Italy Under-21s supremo Silvio Baldini has been in temporary charge after Gennaro Gattuso resigned in April.

Malago and Maldini are plotting to make an appointment before the next international break.

Sports.title: Premier League star immediately gifts grandad World Cup winner’s medal in touching gesture after incredible sacrifice
Sports.content:
PEDRO PORRO fulfilled a lifelong promise by handing his World Cup winner’s medal straight to the man who helped make it all possible.

The Tottenham defender returned home to Spain after lifting football‘s biggest prize – before placing the gold medal around the neck of his proud grandfather Antonio.



Porro later shared the emotional moment on Instagram with the caption: “Misión Cumplida ❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️” – meaning “Mission Accomplished” in Spanish.

And the touching gesture quickly won over fans after it emerged just how much Antonio had sacrificed for his grandson’s career.



As a youngster, Porro’s grandfather drove him thousands of miles across Spain to training sessions and matches as the future Premier League star chased his dream of becoming a professional footballer.

Years later, that dedication was rewarded in the most incredible fashion.



Antonio was pictured beaming with pride while sitting with the World Cup winner’s medal around his neck after Porro returned home.

It capped an unforgettable tournament for the Spurs man, who was named the competition’s best right-back after becoming one of Spain’s standout performers – displacing Atletico Madrid‘s Marcos Llorente after the first match.

Porro had started the World Cup on the bench but forced his way into Luis de la Fuente’s starting XI before becoming one of La Roja’s most important players.

The 26-year-old also played a huge role in Sunday’s dramatic final victory over Argentina.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Operating down the right flank behind teenage sensation Lamine Yamal, Porro whipped in the cross that led to Spain’s extra-time winner.

Nico Williams headed Porro’s delivery back across goal for Ferran Torres to smash home in the 106th minute – a strike that echoed Andres Iniesta’s famous World Cup winning goal against the Netherlands in 2010 as Spain secured a second world title.

Porro also finished the tournament with two goals of his own, including a crucial strike in Spain’s semi-final victory over France.

Speaking after receiving the medal, an emotional Antonio said: “It’s beautiful. This is such a great honor… Now Grandpa has the medal here at home.”



The World Cup triumph continues an trophy-laden rise for Porro, who lifted the Europa League with Tottenham in 2025 before adding football’s biggest prize just a year later.

Sports.title: Chelsea played a blinder beating Arsenal to £117m Morgan Rogers but Blues are gaslighting fans over three major issues
Sports.content:
ON PAPER there are plenty of reasons for Chelsea fans to be cheerful.

A shiny new manager, a big-money signing and – having played a blinder by losing on the last day of the season – no Conference League distraction.



What team wouldn’t be better off with £117million Morgan Rogers?

He’s a super talent and nicking him from under the noses of Arsenal only makes the coup of the summer so far even sweeter.



If Xabi Alonso is going to set Chelsea up as he did at Bayer Leverkusen, with two No 10s behind a striker, the front three of Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Rogers is very tasty.

But they are kicking the can down the road once again when it comes to addressing the real issues that have plagued them – most glaringly the defence, goalkeeper and a distinct lack of experience.



Until those problems are solved, Rogers feels like a luxury signing.

It’s like paying for a brand-spanking-new kitchen and having the bathroom done when the house is built on foundations of jam.

Fans were promised there would be a change of approach this summer – but have Chelsea’s board been gaslighting them?

The top brass insisted they were going to tinker the transfer policy going forwards.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

While not totally abandoning the idea of signing young players on thousand-year contracts to sell on down the line, they said they’d focus on bringing in a more experienced spine to the side. So far, it’s more of the same.

It was evident week after week last season they desperately needed a veteran presence and strong leadership in the dressing room.

Whenever the tide turned against them they folded like a cheap suit and, more often than not, lost their heads.

They had an atrocious disciplinary record with their EIGHT red cards – the most by a side in a Premier League season since QPR racked up nine in the 2011/12 season.

After a promising start, the players quickly turned on boss Liam Rosenior and some were so brazen as to openly court other clubs.



So where is the calming, veteran presence the fans were promised?

One of Chelsea’s best and most experienced players, Marc Cucurella, is gone.

Enzo Fernandez looks likely to follow and they’re trying to flog Trevoh Chalobah.

All the while they’ve shelled out north of £220m for six players, the eldest of which is 23.

Rogers is a fine player with a couple of years of Premier League service but he has thrived with the likes of John McGinn, Ollie Watkins and Youri Tielemans around him.



Chelsea have signed promising full-back Marco Palestra from Atalanta, who had a very good season in Serie A.

But he’s only 21 and has one year of top-flight football under his belt.

Then there’s Geovany Quenda and Emmanuel Emegha, who cost £62m but are unlikely to get near the first team this year.



Clearly, Alonso is aware of the issue that needs addressing, which is why he encouraged the club to try to sign Granit Xhaka – exactly the kind of player Chelsea need.

But the derisory £8m offer for Sunderland’s captain suggested they were never serious.

There have been murmurings from fans that BlueCo weren’t being true to their word, so in recent days they’ve started to get their act together and are trying to sign Crystal Palace’s Maxence Lacroix, 26.

That would finally be a step in the right direction.

They should throw everything at trying to sign England’s World Cup centre-back John Stones, 32, given he is available on a free.



If the Alonso project is to really get off the ground, the club needs to grow up. Literally.

CRYING SHAME

IT IS disheartening to see such an exciting talent as Crysencio Summerville head off to play in Saudi Arabia.

The former West Ham winger had an impressive season in the Premier League last year and shone at the World Cup for the Netherlands.



He was linked with Aston Villa and Roma but ended up joining Al-Hilal.

Just 24, he will spend his peak years in obscurity, in front of tiny crowds.

Clearly the decision is about money but how much is enough? He would have earned a huge packet in Europe – does prestige count for nothing anymore?

RED MIST

JUST when you think things are starting to look up at Old Trafford, the club go and drive another wedge between themselves and their fans.



Manchester United supporters released a scathing statement saying they have been treated like ‘suspects’ after the club suspended thousands of season ticket holder accounts.

United say it’s an attempt to clamp down on touting – but they have tried to resolve a problem which requires surgical precision by deploying a sledgehammer.

Hundreds of loyal – and innocent – fans now have no idea if they will get their season tickets back. It’s yet another dreadful look for the club.



JOOR JOKING

THERE is never a dull week in the world of football agent and major racehorse owner Kia Joorabchian.

Having splashed out tens of millions on a squad of blue-blood thoroughbreds that have looked more like cart-horses this season, he is now engaged in a stand-off with his own jockey.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Joorabchian hired David Egan in 2024 to ride his horses and extended his contract last October.

But a reported bust-up behind the scenes means it looks like Joorabchian will soon be seeking his fourth stable jockey in the last four years.

Sports.title: Arsenal and Tottenham set to go head to head for £51m-rated World Cup star, 21, who faced England
Sports.content:
ARSENAL and Tottenham are preparing to go head-to-head in a fierce transfer battle for RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa.

The Norwegian international, 21, has emerged as one of the most sought-after young attackers in Europe after a stellar spell in the Bundesliga.



Nusa shone at the World Cup, featuring six times and scoring Norway’s first goal in their last-32 win over Ivory Coast.

He was also a second half substitute in his side’s 2-1 extra-time loss to England in the quarter-finals.



SunSport understands that Leipzig are holding firm on a £51million valuation for Nusa, who notched four goals and three assists in 31 Bundesliga appearances last season.

Arsenal are approaching the situation strategically and waiting to assess incoming offers for Gabriel Martinelli before making a formal move.



While the Gunners are not actively pushing to sell Martinelli, a bid exceeding £51m from Europe or Asia could be enough to let the 25-year-old Brazilian go.

Leandro Trossard has already been sold to Besiktas this summer, while Christos Tzolis arrived for £34m from Club Brugge.

Arsenal chief Mikel Arteta missed out on top target Morgan Rogers, with Chelsea sealing a £117m deal.

Neighbours Tottenham are also firmly in the race, but must first clear out their squad before launching an official bid.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Spurs bosses need to resolve the futures of returning loanees Manor Solomon and Mikey Moore, who are both drawing Premier League and Serie A interest.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side have been active in the transfer window already this summer, with Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes signing for £100m and £85m respectively.

Defenders Jan Paul van Hecke – for £52m – and free agents Andy Roberston and Marcos Senesi have also come through the door.

But there is space for a winger, with injured quartet Dejan Kulusevski, Mohammed Kudus, Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert missing Spurs’ pre-season tour to New Zealand and Australia.

The North London rivals face competition from Serie A giants AC Milan and Roma, who have already opened direct talks with Nusa’s representatives.



Milan have made Nusa a priority target and plan to fund the swoop by selling star man Rafael Leao for around £43m, while Roma are ready to test Leipzig’s resolve with a £38m bid.

Nusa is understood to be open to a fresh challenge after a successful World Cup, which could significantly accelerate discussions in the coming weeks.

But the biggest obstacle for all suitors remains negotiating down Leipzig’s steep price tag during upcoming talks.

Sports.title: From plucky minnows to England heroes, Golden Boot showdown and Viking rows… why the 2026 World Cup was greatest ever
Sports.content:
FIFA’S Team of the Tournament features England’s Jude Bellingham, France’s Kylian Mbappe, Argentina’s Lionel Messi . . . and an unlikely hero in Cape Verde ’keeper Vozinha.

The veteran goalie, 40, earned special praise after pulling off a string of eye-catching saves as the minnows suffered a brutal 3-2 defeat to Argentina after extra time.



It was one of the most memorable matches of the tournament, which also featured Viking rowing, a barmy Tartan Army and countless Wayne Rooney one-liners.

The memories of this World Cup linger like Donald Trump on the winner’s podium. The doomsters had predicted a dud. Too many teams, too many hydration breaks and way too expensive in a nation likely to shrug its disinterested collective shoulders.



Fifa greed seemed to be throttling the golden goose. Yet, football, as the old-school managers liked to say, was the winner.

So how will the 2026 tournament be remembered?



Here, are our best moments. . .

1. Keane’s Shakira nod: It all kicked off with Shakira and Burna Boy belting out the official World Cup song Dai Dai at the opening ceremony in Mexico City.

It wouldn’t be a World Cup without Colombian Shakira gyrating in a grass skirt. This was her fourth.

She also performed at the closing ceremony in New York, with ITV analyst Roy Keane revealing a soft spot for the Hips Don’t Lie singer.



To much sniggering from his fellow pundits, Keane said: “It’s always nice to see Shakira.”

2. A brutal group stage: This was supposed to be a damp squib after Fifa expanded the tournament to 48 teams to allow lower- ranked teams to compete. Yet, the minnows defied the odds.

Curacao has a population smaller than Oxford — just 156,000 — and a land mass of just 171 square miles but got a point against Ecuador.



The Democratic Republic of Congo — ranked 46th in the world — held Portugal to a draw before giving England a scare in the Round of 32. While Cape Verde — population 525,000 — advanced to the knock-out stage after a 0-0 draw against Champions-to-be Spain.

Their goalie Vozinha, who wasn’t even contracted to a club, became a hero for his string of saves. In the last 32, he faced off against Lionel Messi and gave Argentina a genuine scare.

3. Beckham’s fishbowl of wine: In the stands to watch Scotland’s trouncing by Brazil in the group stage was David Beckham, who was caught swigging from what one BBC viewer described as a “fishbowl” of red wine.

Another fan said: “Did everyone see Beckham take the biggest swig of red wine from the biggest glass ever?”

4. Victoria’s sour face: Later in the tournament, Becks defended wife Victoria as she failed to celebrate Jude Bellingham’s crucial equaliser in the quarter-final 2-1 win against Norway.



Posh Spice, who was sitting next to her more animated hair-dresser, Ken Paves, seemed to be staring into the mid-distance and not even looking at the pitch.

Former Three Lions skipper David later said: “She was celebrating inside, I promise — her reactions were slightly slower than mine.”

5. Wonderwall: Meanwhile, Oasis’s 1995 hit anthem has become a winner, again. When Wonderwall was first played after England beat Croatia 4-2, the players looked genuinely moved by the fans’ raucous sing-along.

6. The barmy Tartan Army: Scotland fans will never be forgotten in Boston after drinking the city dry, while the Netherlands’ Oranje Army swamped Kansas City in memorable scenes.



5 WINNERS Oasis: Their 1995 hit Wonderwall has re-entered the charts across the globe after being adopted by the England team and fans. Djed Spence: No one had England ace Spence becoming a breakout World Cup star. Cape Verde: A minnow that drew with big fish Spain and also ran Argentina close. Boston Landlords: Thirsty Scotland fans swamped the city for pre-match refreshment, and England fans were also in town. Rodri: Spain star won the Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player. No commentary is complete without a pundit now musing: “Why can’t England produce a midfielder like Rodri?”

7. Tuchel the ‘sex symbol’: If England manager Thomas Tuchel didn’t realise what a white-knuckle ride his job is before the tournament, he does now.

Hailed as a genius for beating Croatia — he told his team at half-time, “If we lose, we lose in our way”.

He even became a Mumsnet sex symbol.

A poster asked whether users of the website found him “strangely attractive,” saying he had a “lovely smile when being interviewed after today’s match”.

One user replied: “He has a certain wiry, athletic, long-limbed vibe to him.”



8. Mexican madness: Then there was the Azteca Stadium in Mexico City.

England secured a dramatic victory after facing the altitude, thunder- storms and a player being sent off.

Defender “Big” Dan Burn came on and headed a ball from his own box to well beyond the halfway line. Again, Tuchel lapped up the plaudits.

Then came the downfall as Tuchel’s game management against Argentina in the semi-final went to pot. But he’ll always have Mumsnet.

9. Anthony Barry: Tuchel’s assistant manager Anthony Barry burst into the national consciousness for his heart-on-the-sleeve half-time interviews.



5 LOSERS Germany: Penalty kings Germany crashed out to Paraguay in the last 32 – on penalties. VAR: The ref-aiding technology became known as VARgentina after it give Lionel Messi’s men a stream of seemingly favourable decisions. Argentina: Standing with their backs to Spain as they collected the World Cup ­trophy was shameful and pathetic. Panama: It was the highest-scoring World Cup tournament ever played, with 308 goals over a record 104 matches. None of them were scored by Panama, the only team that didn’t find the net. Match-Going Fans: Hotels, transport and match tickets were hiked wildly.

Against Croatia, he told viewers that England were “playing with fear”.

As England led France 4-0 in the third place play-off, he said: “I’m a little bit emotional, I can’t find the words about how proud I am of those players.”

10. Wayne Rooney: In the TV studios, Wayne burst on to the scene like he had as a player at Euro 2004.

His summation of the Final’s pop-laden half-time ceremony as “crap” had heads nodding. Over on ITV, Emma Hayes was the stand-out, introducing the word “diagonality” into many people’s footballing lexicon.



11. Gianni’s grin: Fifa chief Gianni Infantino’s grinning mug seemed to stare out from the stands at most games. In fact, he travelled for nearly 60,000 miles to take in 44 matches. On 13 occasions, he went to two matches on the same day.

12. Playing cards: Fifa was accused of “crossing a line” and putting the sport’s integrity into question, after it overturned a ban on the US’s star player Folarin Balogun for a red card.

It emerged that US President Donald Trump had called Infantino and told him the card was “horrible” and that it was “not a foul”.

The US were duly trounced 4-1 by ­Belgium in the quarter-final to ­provide some sporting justice.

The Belgians celebrated, trolling Trump by mimicking his arm-pumping trademark jig.



One social media user dubbed it: “Fantastic s**thousery.”

10 CELEBS Brad Pitt took in several games wearing a USA shirt. Tom Cruise joined the Beckhams for the USA’s match against Paraguay. Jessica Alba took selfies with her daughters at USA v Turkey, which was also watched by Paris Hilton and her kids. Matt Damon was pictured with wife Luciana at the Final as were superstars Jay-Z and Beyonce. The rapper was also at Ivory Coast v Ecuador. Ryan Reynolds cheered on his home country Canada as they played Bosnia & Herzegovina. Sabrina Carpenter watched Ecuador v Germany through opera glasses. Javier Bardem and Penelope Cruz celebrated Spain’s match winner against Belgium. Timothee Chalamet was pictured kissing Kylie Jenner at the Final.

13. Legends assemble: Apart from Ronaldo, who looked ready to join a pensioners’ walking football team, all the other big dogs turned up.

Messi, Mbappe, Bellingham, Haaland, France’s Ousmane Dembele and Harry Kane scrambled to claim the Golden Boot. Kylian triumphed.

14. Haaland the Viking: Erling won over America with his goofy Viking routine as he did Dallas in a Stetson and cowboys boots.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Then he took a stuffed raccoon home on the plane with him.

15. Aggy Argentina: And then there was the Final. If your child’s under-six team behaved like Argentina’s whingeing brats, you’d take the ball off them and send them home.

Sports.title: Conference League clash SUSPENDED for extreme weather with players forced off pitch
Sports.content:
A CONFERENCE League qualifier between Aluminij and Dinamo City was suspended after lightning and torrential rain forced players off the pitch in Slovenia.

Reports in Slovenia confirmed the second qualifying round clash at Ljudski Vrt was halted in the 55th minute after dangerous weather swept across the stadium.



Both teams, coaching staff and the match officials immediately retreated to the dressing rooms and tunnel as lightning strikes were detected in the area.

The visitors held a narrow 1-0 lead when play was stopped, with the weather making it unsafe for the match to continue.



Updates posted on X confirmed the suspension was caused by “adverse weather”, with heavy rain and lightning striking close to the ground.

Supporters inside the stadium were left waiting as officials monitored conditions before deciding whether it was safe for the game to resume.

Fortunately, the delay lasted only around 20 minutes.

A further update confirmed the match had resumed once the storm had passed over the stadium.

Dinamo City returned to the pitch still protecting their slender advantage over the Slovenian hosts.

The Albanian side had taken the lead after just 15 minutes when Hekuran Berisha capitalised on a huge defensive mistake.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Aluminij defender Dino Šimunić under-hit a back pass towards goalkeeper Florijan Radu, allowing Berisha to intercept before rounding the keeper and calmly slotting into an empty net.

It proved to be the only shot on target of the opening half as Aluminij struggled to create chances.

Reports in Slovenia also noted the hosts had failed to score in an official match for more than 500 minutes heading into the contest.

But they did find a late equaliser to earn a 1-1 draw and make it all to play for in the second leg in Tirana.

Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Alex Scott final decision made as £100m transfer target back on the radar

Manchester United round-up as a big decision is made on a transfer target

View 3 Images Alex Scott has been linked with Manchester United (Image: AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images)

A crucial summer is underway at Manchester United as the club look to build on the progress made under Michael Carrick over the second half of last season. With Champions League football to look forward to, United needed to strengthen to cope with the increased demands on the squad.

‌



Midfield was - and remains - a priority area. Progress has already been made in that department, with Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans arriving from Chelsea and Aston Villa, respectively. France World Cup Manu Kone is on the radar, as is Alex Scott, who recently rejected a new contract offer from Bournemouth.

‌



Meanwhile, the future of Marcus Rashford remains up in the air after Barcelona opted against triggering their option to buy him. As it stands, Rashford, who is currently on a post-World Cup break, will rejoin United, potentially during August's training camp in Ireland, which includes a friendly against Leeds in Dublin.

‌



Here's a round-up of the latest news as Carrick looks to put his stamp on the squad ahead of his first full season in charge….

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Scott decision made

United have pulled out of the race to sign Scott after being priced out of a move for the midfielder. The Red Devils' valuation of £40million differs greatly from the £70m Bournemouth are seeking.

‌



Marcus Rashford will have to confront awkward Man Utd reality when he returns to Old Trafford READ MORE :

Arsenal, Manchester City and Tottenham are interested in the player, while Chelsea have reportedly had a £64m offer rejected. Scott has two years left on the contract he signed when joining from Bristol City for £25m in 2023.

View 3 Images United have shelved their interest in Scott (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

United revisit £100m target

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Gunners move for £94m Morgan Rogers alternative as transfer announcement made
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Gunners move for £94m Morgan Rogers alternative as transfer announcement made

Mikel Arteta is looking to make up for a sluggish start to Arsenal's summer transfer window

View 2 Images Arsenal have officially announced the signing of forward Christos Tzolis (Image: Getty )

Arsenal are finally accelerating their transfer activity as they look to lay down a marker in an uninspired summer window until now. Mikel Arteta, having guided the Gunners to a long-awaited Premier League triumph and the Champions League final, insisted that top quality new signings were required at the end of last season.

‌



So far, sporting director Andrea Berta has under-delivered on that promise despite reportedly being handed a gargantuan transfer budget potentially exceeding £250million. Arsenal’s first official signing was making Piero Hincapie’s move a permanent one last month.

‌



They followed that up by confirming the arrival of back-up goalkeeper Illan Meslier. However, the Gunners are still yet to upgrade in several key positions, including defence, central-midfield and left-wing.

‌



Failed pursuits of several long-term targets, including Jeremy Monga and Morgan Rogers, have done little to alleviate concerns among fans, with the pair joining rivals Manchester City and Chelsea respectively.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

On the sales front, Berta still hasn’t found clubs for several players who are surplus to requirements at the Emirates Stadium. However, Mirror Football now takes a look at two promising transfer updates involving the north London club.

‌



Christos Tzolis announcement

Arsenal have announced the signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge. The 24-year-old Greece international has penned a five-year deal following his £34m transfer to north London.

Tzolis faced Arsenal during their Champions League league phase clash with Brugge last season. While he didn’t score on that occasion, the winger managed an incredible 51 goal involvements in 52 appearances for the side over the course of the season.

He will wear the No.17 shirt and is seen as a long-term replacement for Leandro Trossard, who joined Besiktas last week. "It's absolutely amazing to sign for such a big club, the champions of England. I'm very proud to be part of this team for the next season," the winger said.

‌



"When my agent was saying maybe it was a possibility, I was already excited. Afterwards it was getting more serious and now I'm here. I had a nice conversation [with Mikel Arteta]. It was around an hour. We talked about everything, about the club, about myself, about his plans, about me of course, about the team. It was only positive things."

Yan Diomande enquiry

View 2 Images Yan Diomande is believed to cost around £94m (Image: Michael Miller/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Arsenal are reportedly eyeing Yan Diomande as an alternative to Rogers after missing out on the England star. The Gunners’ need for a marquee left-wing signing remains at the top of their agenda, with a move for RB Leipzig ace Diomande now being considered.

‌



football.london reports that Arsenal have made an enquiry for the 19-year-old sensation, who impressed at the World Cup with his dazzling displays for Ivory Coast. The report states the English champions have voiced their desire to be kept informed of the conditions surrounding the Ivorian.

Arsenal valued Rogers at around £80m but fell short of Aston Villa’s valuation of the midfielder, which led to them losing out on his signature to Chelsea, who instead completed the deal for £117m. Diomande is expected to cost around £94m this summer, with Liverpool already seeing an £85m bid for the player rejected.

Diomande is claimed to favour a transfer to PSG but the European champions have not yet met Leipzig’s asking price either. Arsenal’s enquiry is believed to have been purely exploratory at the time and the club have not advanced from there so far during the transfer window.

Sports.title: Jermain Defoe leaves first managerial job after SIX games - 'Impossible to continue'
Sports.content:
Jermain Defoe leaves first managerial job after SIX games - 'Impossible to continue'

Jermain Defoe took his first step into management with National League side Woking at the end of March, but the ex-England's striker reign has already come to an end

View 2 Images Jermain Defoe released a statement following his exit (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

Jermain Defoe's first job as a manager has come an end after just four months. National League side Woking announced on Thursday that they'd parted ways with the Premier League icon, who said in a statement that it was 'impossible to continue'.

‌



Defoe, 43, was appointed at the end of March and guided Woking to a 10th-place finish in the fifth tier. The ex-England striker won two of his six games in charge and was expected to lead the Surrey outfit into the 2026-27 season.

‌



But Woking announced on Thursday evening that his reign has come to an end. The club said: "Woking Football Club can confirm that the club and First Team Manager Jermain Defoe have mutually agreed to part ways with immediate effect.

‌



"We would like to place on record our sincere thanks to Jermain for his contribution during his time at Woking Football Club, and we wish him every success in the future. The club remains fully focused on delivering its objectives both on and off the pitch. We would like to thank our supporters for their continued support."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

FA release statement after video of England team-mates fighting goes viral READ MORE :

Defoe then issued a statement of his own on social media. The 43-year-old explained: "Following recent discussions, I can confirm that I have mutually agreed to leave my position as manager of Woking FC.

‌



"Unfortunately, circumstances have ultimately made it impossible for me to continue in the position. I am extremely proud of the work undertaken during my time at the club and genuinely felt that we were building something special.

"I would like to thank Todd Johnson for giving me the opportunity to manage the club. I am incredibly grateful to the supporters and, most importantly, the players, who I am genuinely gutted for. The group is a fantastic one, and I wish the squad every success for the season ahead.

Which current Premier League star would make the best manager? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Jermain Defoe lasted four months at Woking (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

"I'm really disappointed the journey has ended so soon, but I leave with great pride in what Paul Bracewell, Karl Halabi and I were building at the club.

"My time at Woking FC has been an eye-opening managerial experience and one that will undoubtedly make me stronger for the next challenge in my career."

‌



Defoe took charge of two pre-season friendlies, as Woking faced non-league side Sholing before taking on Portsmouth, one of his former clubs. The Tottenham hero worked as a coach in Spurs' academy for two years before leaving in 2024 to pursue his first head coach role.

That arrived in March with Woking sitting 11th. The Cardinals had sacked Neal Ardley, with ambitions of finishing inside the play-offs. Woking will now look to appoint a new manager in time for the National League season which stars on Saturday, August 8.

Sports.title: Man Utd identify World Cup star as new target after pulling out of Alex Scott transfer
Sports.content:
Man Utd identify World Cup star as new target after pulling out of Alex Scott transfer

Manchester United want to sign a third midfielder before the summer transfer window closes but they've been priced out of a move for Bournemouth star Alex Scott

View 2 Images Danilo played for Brazil at the World Cup (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Manchester United are weighing up a move for ex-Nottingham Forest star Danilo. The news comes after United decided not to pursue a deal for Bournemouth's Alex Scott.

‌



Bournemouth will demand at least £70million for Scott, who was the subject of a £64m bid from Chelsea which was rejected earlier this week. United value the England international at around £40m and will now look at alternative options in their search for a third new central midfielder.

‌



BBC Sport report that the Red Devils have registered their interest in Danilo, who plays for Brazilian side Botafogo. It's added that Newcastle were interested in the 25-year-old earlier this summer.

‌



Danilo made four appearances at the World Cup - all from the bench - as part of Carlo Ancelotti's squad. Botafogo have already received two offers in the region of £25m from Brazilian rivals Palmeiras and Russian heavyweights Zenit St Petersburg.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd given green light for Aurelien Tchouameni transfer as Real Madrid stance emerges READ MORE :

Palmeiras, where Danilo made his name over three seasons, are currently pushing hardest to complete a deal. Botafogo would prefer sell him abroad, having paid £21.7m to sign him from Forest a year ago.

‌



Danilo is one of several options for United, who've also enquired about Real Madrid midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni. The Red Devils have already recruited two midfielders this summer; Andrey Santos for £50m and Youri Tielemans for £35m.

In two-and-a-half years with Forest, Danilo made 62 appearances across all competitions. His third season at the City Ground was blighted by a serious ankle injury which took a toll on him.

Which midfielder should Manchester United sign? Have your say in the comments section.

‌

"It was really tough at first, but with time it got easier," Danilo told FIFA's website before the World Cup. "I started to understand things differently. I matured a lot.

"I became stronger and learned to think more positively every day. After that injury, I developed this mindset."

Article continues below

Botafogo are having a middling season, sitting 10th in the Brazilian top flight with seven wins, four draws and seven defeats after 18 games. Danilo has been prolific in front of goal, though, scoring seven league goals as well as three in cup competitions.

Sports.title: Man Utd given green light for Aurelien Tchouameni transfer as Real Madrid stance emerges
Sports.content:
Man Utd given green light for Aurelien Tchouameni transfer as Real Madrid stance emerges

Manchester United are interested in signing Aurelien Tchouameni from Real Madrid, lodging an enquiry as they bid to revamp their midfield in the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Aurelien Tchouameni is a target for Manchester United (Image: Stephen Nadler/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Real Madrid are open to selling Aurelien Tchouameni in a major boost to Manchester United's chances of signing him. Tchouameni, 26, has just got back from helping France reach the semi-finals of the World Cup, playing an integral role in Didier Deschamps' side.

‌



But throughout the tournament, his future at club level was a hot topic. United have a long-standing interest in Tchouameni, who Real boss Jose Mourinho initially planned to keep after returning to the Bernabeu this summer.

‌



However, the Sun report that Real are now prepared to let the midfielder go at the right price. The La Liga giants have been linked with a big-money move for Manchester City star Rodri and might need to drum up funds.

‌



United's interest is said to have ramped up since the World Cup ended, with Tchouameni out of contract in 2028. It was reported in Spain earlier this month that Real and the Frenchman had agreed a new five-year deal, although there's been no confirmation.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Manchester United pull out of Alex Scott transfer race after learning asking price READ MORE :

United have already signed two midfielders this summer, paying a combined £85m for Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. But with Manuel Ugarte expected to miss most of the season because of a serious knee injury, the Red Devils want to add a third.

‌



Their search for a specialist defensive midfielder has led them to Tchouameni, whose experience of starting the 2022 World Cup final and winning the Champions League in 2024 appeals to United. The former Monaco star also suits United's preferred age range for signings - between 22 and 26.

How much should Manchester United pay for Aurelien Tchouameni? Have your say in the comments section.

Real's pursuit of Rodri could therefore prove to be a double boost for United, as local rivals City would be losing one of their best players. However, Los Blancos could wait until Rodri's contract expires next summer and sign him on a free.

As for Tchouameni, ex-Real midfielder and French compatriot Claude Makelele has warned Bernabeu chiefs not to sell him. Makelele told DAZN: "He was the only player who performed consistently from start to finish.

"Mourinho isn't a fool; he's a good manager, one of the best managers. He knows he's going to need a strong squad to be able to win La Liga."

Sports.title: Arsenal to launch £70m Bruno Guimaraes bid - but transfer for Newcastle star hangs in balance
Sports.content:
Arsenal to launch £70m Bruno Guimaraes bid - but transfer for Newcastle star hangs in balance

Bruno Guimaraes has emerged as a top target for Arsenal this summer in their search for quality reinforcements and they are ready to pay out £70million to sign him

View 2 Images Arsenal want to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle (Image: Getty )

Arsenal are poised to table a £70million bid for Bruno Guimaraes - but will not overpay for the midfielder if Newcastle try to resist a sale.

‌



The Gunners are in the market for quality additions to bolster the squad that won the Premier League and reached the Champions League final last season. And a move for Guimaraes, who boasts extensive top-flight pedigree, appeals in their search for an elite midfielder.

‌



Guimaraes, 28, is known to be keen on the move, which would give him a realistic opportunity to win major trophies.

‌



Newcastle, though, have no appetite to cash in on their talismanic captain — and it remains to be seen if a financial package in the region of £70m would realistically be enough for them to soften that stance.

BBC Sport report that Arsenal are ready to launch an official bid of that amount after stepping up their interest in Guimaraes. However, it's noted that they will not stray from their valuation of the Brazilian.

Whether or not they would consider bidding higher for a player who turns 29 later this year remains to be seen. And if that is the case, then they could opt to move on to other targets.

‌



That stance saw them miss out on a deal for Morgan Rogers, a long-term target who was viewed as the ceiling-raiser signing Arsenal were looking for in their search for a new left-sided attacker.

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes wants to join Arsenal this summer (Image: Getty Images)

The Gunners valued Rogers at £80m; a figure far lower than Aston Villa's valuation of the England star. That gulf in valuations opened the door for Chelsea to swoop in with a £117m offer. Arsenal declined to match it, with Rogers going on to join one of their big domestic rivals.

Article continues below

Rogers' former Aston Villa team-mate, Ezri Konsa, is another player Arsenal are courting with the new Premier League season now just weeks away.

Sports.title: Argentina's shameful behaviour should not let the World Cup's biggest offenders off the hook
Sports.content:
Argentina's shameful behaviour should not let the World Cup's biggest offenders off the hook

Lionel Messi and his beaten Argentina team-mates deserved all the flak that came their way following the World Cup final but that should not give Gianni Infantino and FIFA a reprieve

View 3 Images Lionel Messi has come under fire for his behaviour in the World Cup final (Image: Getty Images)

According to a polling company that might have better things to do, Lionel Messi’s popularity amongst British people has gone down since he tried to get the saintly Marc Cucurella sent off during the World Cup final. It is unclear whether this news is keeping Messi awake at night but you suspect not.

‌



Messi’s lamentable attempt to land Cucurella in trouble was part of a tapestry of unedifying Argentinian antics and was unbecoming of a great player. But it was hardly the crime of the century.

‌



Since when did we become so puritanical? Would Cucurella have done it if the situation of the game had been reversed? Of course he would.

‌



You might hold Messi to a higher moral standard but players trying to get opponents into bother is a staple of the modern game. It did not help Messi’s cause that he was the captain of a squad that turned its back on Spain’s coronation after it had also descended into violent disarray at the final whistle.

Argentina flop's sister makes Falklands Islands claim after World Cup shame READ MORE :

The offending individuals will deserve whatever punishment comes their way and deserved all the criticism that has already come their way. But let’s not pretend we were shocked by the Argentinian reaction to the loss to Spain.

And let’s not allow their behaviour to deflect criticism and scrutiny from where it most needs to be directed most. It needs to be directed most at Gianni Infantino and FIFA.

‌



View 3 Images Bryson DeChambeau threatened to get Donald Trump involved in his rules row at The Open (Image: Richard Heathcote, Getty Images)

When it comes to petulant reactions, there was a belter at Royal Birkdale last Friday after Bryson DeChambeau received a two-shot penalty for what was a debatable rules infringement. It was a slightly controversial decision but one DeChambeau should have taken on the chin.

Instead, he ranted and raved at officials … and, apparently, threatened to call Donald Trump and get him involved. As it happened, the President of the United States never stepped in but you know where the idea came from.

‌



Thankfully, at least one football association is taking a stance. The Norwegians, headed by its federation president Lise Klaveness, are set to make an official complaint to FIFA’s ethics committee over Trump’s involvement in the Folarin Balogun case, which saw the American striker have his red card ban suspended.

View 3 Images Messi has been accused of trying to get Marc Cucurella sent off (Image: AFP or licensors)

Hopefully, more will follow suit. And hopefully, more will tell the relevant committee that the hydration breaks were aberrations that cannot be repeated. Hopefully, more will kick up a serious fuss over ticket prices and already demand changes for the 2030 World Cup.

‌



Never mind the tantrums shown by several Argentinians after the last whistle - and it has to be said that we seem to be more upset by them than the Spanish are - the final itself was a grotesquely gaudy and elongated occasion. Wayne Rooney had it spot on when he said the best thing about the half-time show was when it finished.

Sure, Argentina’s behaviour needs to be punished. And sure, Messi did not cover himself in glory. But the people who really need to be looked at now the World Cup is over are Infantino and FIFA.

Sports.title: 'Good luck to Dirk...': Littler dazzles in Blackpool as 'frightening' form continues
Sports.content:
If a player hit a nine-darter on the World Matchplay stage, that would usually go down as their highlight. That is just the tip of the iceberg for Luke Littler in 2026.

Littler came into Blackpool as the reigning and defending champion with the expectations on his shoulders to deliver.

He has and then some. The numbers are jaw-dropping:

113 average in first round (second-highest at Matchplay behind Phil Taylor's 114.99 in 2010)

109 average in second round and quarter-finals

Nine-darter vs Nathan Aspinall

17 180s vs Josh Rock

14 180s vs Nathan Aspinall

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the quarter-final between Luke Littler and Josh Rock

If his heights were not already incomprehensible, they have gone up a notch.

Not only that, Littler knows he can dominate.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Littler admits he's playing some of the best darts of his career after a dominant win over Rock

"I feel really good up on the stage. Preparations beforehand have gone really well, just relaxing, playing and relaxing again. I am just glad I can perform on the biggest stages," Littler said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the thrilling second-round match between Littler and Nathan Aspinall

"I feel like I can. Obviously a 109 average, a 113 and back down to a 109 average comes with the big finishes. The scoring power is there as well.

"As long as I can keep it up, I'm sure I will dominate. Next game, let's get it back up to the 113s."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Littler produced an incredible nine-darter in the opening leg of his match with Aspinall

That next game will see Dirk van Duijvenbode become the next player charged with attempting to stop Littler in his tracks.

Up to this point, Littler's win over Rock marked the 27th time in a row he won a match that went over 20 legs.

Not only that, Littler continues his quest to become the first player since Michael van Gerwen in 2016 to go back-to-back in Blackpool, and the world No 1 currently holds the World Darts Championship, UK Open, Premier League and Masters. He is also defending the Matchplay, Grand Slam, Grand Prix and the Players Championship Finals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aspinall offers up his darts to the crowd after Littler almost hits his second nine-darter of the match

With all the in mind, Sky Sports Darts' Mark Webster has a simple message for the Dutchman when he takes on the best player in the world on Saturday, live on Sky Sports: "Good luck."

"He can play in spells. I say spells because he's been doing it all tournament. I was delighted for Josh because it was an improved performance and a 101 average but he lost by nine legs so it just shows how good Littler is," Webster said.

"He looks comfortable in every scenario. Good luck to Dirk on Saturday.

"It's 111 tournament average. He's played almost 60 legs. He's just too good! He's focused and relaxed.

"He's by far the best player in the world. It's frightening form."

Image: Littler is producing some stunning stats at the World Matchplay

It was revealed in May that the three-time Grand Slam champion had joined Draper's team, after Draper had split with his former coach Jamie Delgado.
