Sports.title: MALISHEVA 2 HIBERNIAN 0: Humiliation for Hibs as David Gray's Leith men fall to Kosovans in Conference League qualification
Sports.content:
Hibernian’s quest for Conference League football is in jeopardy after a humbling by unfancied Kosovan outfit Malisheva.

Kreshnik Uka stunned David Gray’s side in the first leg of the second qualifying tie at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium in Pristina when he opened the scoring in the 21st minute from close range.

Hibs stepped up the pressure after the break and new signing Nathan Lowe missed a couple of chances as they chased a precious equaliser but home substitute Valjmir Nafiu added a second in the 90th minute on the break to leave the Scots with a rescue mission in the second leg at Easter Road next week.

Gray and his men were roundly booed by the travelling fans who had made the journey to eastern Europe and the Hibs boss conceded they had let down their supporters.

And despite being second best throughout a miserable 90 minutes, the Easter Road boss insisted his men could turn the tie around in Leith next week.

‘We were way below the requirement and the expectations of this football club,’ conceded Gray. ‘I know that, and it’s a reflection on myself and the team.

Hibs defenders Felix Passlack and Adam Mayor reflect on a night to forget for the visitors

‘I’m not going to stand here and try and justify it or make excuses at all. We weren’t good enough.

‘The only positive, if there is anything to come out of today, is the fact it’s happened in the first leg and there is still an opportunity to turn it around — and I do believe we are good enough to do it from what I’ve seen today.

‘Fans will certainly not want to hear apologies. The support was incredible today. They have spent their money to come and watch the team and we know we’ve let them down.

‘I wasn’t shocked or surprised by anything I saw from the opposition, what we expected going into the game. We know that they’re an aggressive side, a team that will do the transition quickly — the second goal is another example of that.

‘Everything that could have gone wrong for us today certainly did and it’s very hard to win games of football when there’s so many of us not at the level required.

‘That wasn’t just one or two players. To win any game of football at any level, never mind European football, you need to have a level of performance that’s good enough throughout the team.

‘I don’t think there’s a single player today that can hold their hand up and say, I was at the very best of my ability today.

‘But I still firmly believe in the group. The criticism and everything is going to come and rightly so but there’s only one person who can try and turn it around and it’s my responsibility to make sure the team are right and ready for next week.’

Kreshnik Uka converts the opener to give the Kosovan side a deserved first-half lead

It was another abject night for Scottish football in Europe as the Leith side came up short against a club that is only a decade old.

On-loan Stoke striker Lowe was the only new signing in Gray’s side for the first competitive game of the season.

Hibs, who secured their European place with a fifth-placed finish in the Premiership last season, looked comfortable enough in the early stages in front of a sparse crowd.

In the seventh minute forward Owen Elding had a looping header from a Felix Passlack cross cleared off the line by Malisheva captain Dreni Kryeziu, with keeper Ilir Avdyli beaten.

The home side showed little in attack until the 15th minute when midfielder Arlind Veliu had an effort from inside the Hibs box deflected over the bar for a corner which came to nothing.

However, Malisheva kept pushing and when Veliu made his way down the left and cut the ball back into the box, Dzemal Ibishi missed the first contact but Uka stabbed the ball low past Hibs goalkeeper Raphael Sallinger.

Hibs’ response was lukewarm, notwithstanding a header from defender Grant Hanley that was easily saved by Avdyli.

Adam Mayor, Hibs’ summer signing from Millwall, replaced Jack Iredale for the second half and the Edinburgh side enjoyed more of the ball and put on some pressure.

Hibs boss David Gray remains confident his side can turn the tie around at Easter Road

Lowe, who scored in the win over Brondby last weekend, hit the outside of the post and went close again when he found himself through on goal in the 51st minute. Zambian midfielder Miguel Chaiwa soon blazed an effort over the bar following a corner.

The visitors kept pushing and in the 66th minute Lowe raced clear but missed the target with an unconvincing drive.

At the other end, Sallinger was pleased to see a header from Donart Vitija land in his arms.

The game became disjointed and scrappy in the final stages but Hibs were again stunned in the final minute of normal time when Nafiu fired high into the net after being brilliantly set up by Uka on the counter.

Gray’s side now have it all to do in the return game at home next week.

Malisheva (3-5-2): Avdyli; Shani (Murati 72), Kryeziu, Skovgaard; Isgandarli (Pira 72), Vitija (Luma 86), Ferati, Uka, Veliu; Ibishi (Bajraktari 92), Xhylani (Nafiu 71). Booked: None. Manager: Thomas Brdaric.

Hibernian (4-3-3): Sallinger; Passlack, O’Hora, Hanley, Iredale (Mayor 46); Mulligan (Abdulai 81), Chaiwa, Obita; Elding (Newell 68), Lowe, Boyle (Klidje 68). Booked: O’Hora, Abdulai. Manager: David Gray.

Sports.title: Donald Trump's Folarin Balogun red card intervention scandal takes fresh twist as match-fixing watchdog flags controversial reversal
Sports.content:
Donald Trump's Folarin Balogun red card intervention scandal takes fresh twist as match-fixing watchdog flags controversial reversal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A gambling watchdog group has flagged the United States' Round-of-16 loss to Belgium as one of seven World Cup matches that may have drawn irregular betting activity during the tournament.

Specifically, the independent Group of Copenhagen cited a predictions market line titled 'Will Folarin Balogun play against Belgium?' as one potential issue, sources told The Athletic.

That line opened on July 2 shortly after Balogun was given a controversial red card in Team USA's Round-of-32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina. On July 5, after President Donald Trump urged FIFA to rescind Balogun's red card, the governing body opted instead to suspend his one-game ban until after the tournament, thereby allowing him to play in the loss to Belgium.

Curiously, the Group of Copenhagen's report specified that no other similar markets opened for the 14 other players who got a red card during the tournament, according to The Athletic. Now the group has requested an official explanation from FIFA on the Balogun case.

The Daily Mail has sought comment from both FIFA and Polymarket, neither of which have been accused of any misconduct in this case.

Operating under the Council of Europe's Macolin Convention of 2014, the Group of Copenhagen is an independent network that detects and prevents the manipulation of sports competitions around the world. For the 2026 World Cup, the organization reviewed all 104 matches from the tournament, which attracted more than $240 billion bets worldwide, according to the Group of Copenhagen.

Folarin Balogun (20) fouls Bosnia's Tarik Muharemovic (4), resulting in a red card

Balogun was given a controversial red card in Team USA's Round-of-32 win over Bosnia

Although its full report has not yet been published, a summary of its conclusions has been shared by the Council of Europe.

The US loss to Belgium was among seven 'yellow notices' raised by the Group of Copenhagen, which has two higher levels of concern: orange and red.

'The Group of Copenhagen's notices can be explained by atypical behaviors such as changes in odds or hedging liquidities, there are many explanations that are not manipulations,' Christian Kalb, a gambling industry expert who previously worked with the Group of Copenhagen, told The Athletic.

'The major problem is when there may be a conflict of interest and potential inside information on those issues,' she continued. 'When we speak of prediction markets, we can detect some unusual behaviors but we must be very careful as they can be used for hedging markets.

The Norwegian FA is planning to complain to FIFA over the Folarin Balogun World Cup saga

Meanwhile, the Norwegian FA plans to launch a formal complaint to FIFA over Trump's interference in Balogun's red card ban.

Despite Trump's interventions, the US were thrashed 4-1 by Belgium, yet the 80-year-old has repeatedly boasted about his involvement, adding that FIFA President Gianni Infantino made a 'great decision.'

The antics of Trump and FIFA were widely condemned across the sport, and Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) President Lise Klaveness now says she is planning to formally complain to the governing body's ethics committee.

'When you bend a rule like this, you're on a slippery slope that will put the whole game at risk,' she said. 'It is a worry for the game when you compromise fundamental rules of the game.

'First of all, it should not have happened. It is very important now to have honest communication around it. We all know that this verdict was influenced from external forces and did not have the proper process.

'If you start to adapt in such a way towards state leaders and state politics, you will move your behavior and the organization's behavior, and also the red line of what states' leaders should interfere with. And that happened.'

Defending his role in the saga, Infantino insisted it was an independent decision taken by FIFA's disciplinary committee.

He said: 'They operate autonomously, apply the FIFA's disciplinary code, and decide cases based on the applicable regulations and the specific facts before them.

'Their independence is essential to the credibility and integrity of football, and this must always be respected.'

Sports.title: Jermain Defoe walks away from Woking after less than four months in charge: Ex-England star fails to take training before abruptly QUITTING amid clash with member of club management
Sports.content:
Jermain Defoe has walked away from National League Woking after just four months in charge.

Defoe managed six competitive matches at Woking and had been preparing the side for the new season but has abruptly quit his role.

Sources have told Daily Mail Sport that Defoe did not turn up to take training on Thursday and later called the club to inform them he would be stepping down.

One source indicated there was internal conflict between Defoe and a member of the Woking hierarchy. The National League club have declined to comment any further.

The former Spurs striker lost just one of his six games in charge, as the Surrey-based outfit finished tenth in the fifth tier.

In a statement, Woking said: ‘Woking Football Club can confirm that the club and First Team Manager Jermain Defoe have mutually agreed to part ways with immediate effect.

Jermain Defoe (left) has left his role as Woking manager after less than five months in charge

‘We would like to place on record our sincere thanks to Jermain for his contribution during his time at Woking Football Club, and we wish him every success in the future.

‘The club remains fully focused on delivering its objectives both on and off the pitch. We would like to thank our supporters for their continued support.’

Posting on Instagram, Defoe said: 'Following recent discussions, I can confirm that I have mutually agreed to leave my position as manager of Woking FC. Unfortunately, circumstances have ultimately made it impossible for me to continue in the position.

'I am extremely proud of the work undertaken during my time at the club and genuinely felt that we were building something special.

'I would like to thank Todd Johnson for giving me the opportunity to manage the club. I am incredibly grateful to the supporters and, most importantly, the players, who I am genuinely gutted for. The group is a fantastic one, and I wish the squad every success for the season ahead.

'Really disappointed the journey has ended so soon, but I leave with great pride in what Paul Bracewell, Karl Halabi and I were building at the club.

'My time at Woking FC has been an eye-opening managerial experience and one that will undoubtedly make me stronger for the next challenge in my career.’

Sports.title: 'Traumatic experience' - Kiwi sailing superstar sets sights on successful comeback in Portsmouth
Sports.content:
'Traumatic experience' - Kiwi sailing superstar sets sights on successful comeback in Portsmouth

The world's best sailors are descending on the south coast this weekend as the SailGP season continues.

View Image Women's Performance Session at SailGP Technologies ahead of the Emirates Great Britain Sail Grand Prix.

After their explosive start to the SailGP season was derailed by an enormous crash and a horror injury, Liv Mackay and Black Foils are hoping to hit the comeback trail at the Emirates Great Britain Sail Grand Prix in Portsmouth this weekend.

‌



The Kiwis lost control of their F50 in gusty conditions in front of their home crowd in Auckland, crashing into the French boat and leaving grinder Louis Sinclair with compound fractures in both legs following a sickening crash.

‌



But after their return to the water and competitive action last time out in Halifax, Canada, Mackay believes this weekend’s Portsmouth race – which will see the world's best athletes compete in close-to-shore, short races at speeds of more than 100km/h – can be the perfect reset.

‌



She said: “It was definitely the most traumatic experience I've ever had. There was a huge crowd, big grandstands, and it was obviously a home event. We'd been doing really well in the first two races and had a really good energy about it.

“But the crash itself was a loss of control of the boat, and we weren't able to regain that control on the breach. And unfortunately, when we did regain some sense of control we got hit. The whole experience was very short but long.

“Louis was stuck in the water and that was probably the most traumatic thing about all of it for quite some time. We were very fortunate that he didn't panic. He was very calm.”

‌



Thanks to months out with a broken boat, Black Foils currently sit 12th in the 13-team strong championship, leaving them targeting individual races rather than the overall standings.

But last year, they finished third across the championship, racking up more points than second placed Bonds Flying Roos, thanks to a memorable victory in Portsmouth.

Mackay said: “We're definitely a bit rusty when sailing together. But it's always a good feeling when you come back to where you won before, and it does bring back good memories, which is really nice.

‌



“There are a lot of Kiwis that live in England. A lot of my family's actually from England, so there are really strong ties here. The weather forecast is looking nice and windy, which is always fun. So yes, I'd say it's a pretty good feeling.”

The 30-year-old is the Black Foils’ strategist and competes alongside male counterparts in SailGP’s rare gender-integrated competition.

Emirates GBR may be the reigning world champions - and will be looking to get a home win in front of a sold-out crowd this weekend but the Kiwis have other ideas.

‌



Portsmouth is just about as far as you can get from Mackay’s childhood upbringing in rural New Zealand, but it won’t curb her enthusiasm in Portsmouth.

She said: “We are excited about this weekend, and we want to make our mark – we will be competitive.

“Most of our team members are actually from more rural parts of New Zealand. I definitely think it brings a different side to it, which is quite fun and makes us closer as a group.

Article continues below

“My parents didn't sail so my route into sailing was quite different to the typical one. I think it really shows my love for the sport. And my brother's the same. It's just a genuine journey. There's been no pressure.

“Our team is very proud of who we are as Kiwis. Being from different parts of New Zealand brings a unique team together.”

The Emirates Great Britain Sail Grand Prix returns to Portsmouth on 25-26 July. Limited tickets are still available via //SailGP.com/Portsmouth

Sports.title: Katarina Johnson-Thompson pulls out of Commonwealth Games as Team England reshuffles squad
Sports.content:
Katarina Johnson-Thompson pulls out of Commonwealth Games as Team England reshuffles squad

Katarina Johnson-Thompson's hopes of winning a historic third successive Commonwealth Games heptathlon title are over after the Team England star has opted to prioritise next month's European Athletics Championships instead.

View Image Katarina Johnson-Thompson will not defend her Commonwealth Games heptathlon title after withdrawing from Team England's squad.

Katarina Johnson-Thompson's bid for a historic third consecutive Commonwealth Games title is over before it has even begun. Johnson-Thompson is thought to have prioritised her bid for a first-ever European title in Birmingham next month and will be replaced by Niamh Emerson.

‌



The prospect of two home major championships in the space of a fortnight always meant difficult choices for British athletes. These Games were originally scheduled for March until Australia withdrew as hosts and Glasgow stepped in with just 18 months' notice.

‌



In addition to Johnson-Thompson, fellow Olympic medallists Dina Asher-Smith, Daryll Neita, Amber Anning and Matthew Hudson-Smith have all now confirmed they will miss the Games, with the team for the Europeans due to be named on Monday. Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson has always said Glasgow was not part of their plans for this season.

‌



Selection for Glasgow continues a remarkable comeback year for the 27-year-old Emerson, who completed her first heptathlon in eight years in April.

Emerson, who was previously mentored by Jessica Ennis-Hill, was tipped as the sport's next big thing after winning the world junior title in 2018, the same year she claimed Commonwealth bronze on the Gold Coast.

Asher-Smith is replaced by Renee Regis in the 4x100m relay squad, joining her sister Alicia, a member of the 4x400m team. Their selection comes 36 years after their father, John Regis, and mother, Jenny Stoute, both won Commonwealth gold in Auckland.

‌



"I wish the athletes the very best of luck in their recoveries and with the opportunities ahead during the rest of their seasons," said athletics team leader Scott Grace.

"This is a fantastic opportunity for athletes who are in excellent form to step into Team England and represent their country on the world stage. We are excited to support these athletes in Glasgow over the next couple of weeks."

Team England's athletics squad will now be headlined by world medallists Amy Hunt and Georgia Hunter Bell, who pulled out of last weekend's Diamond League meeting through illness.

‌



Hunt, who won 200m world silver in Tokyo, will compete in the 100m in Glasgow before doubling up in both sprint events in Birmingham.

"I think I'm always a bit of a dark horse going into championships, so no matter what's happened during my season, people should never write me off," said Hunt.

"At Christmas I wrote down my goals, and now I'm starting to think, 'Wow, maybe we can chase those.’"

Sports.title: Katarina Johnson-Thompson and eight other stars pull out of Commonwealth Games in major blow
Sports.content:
Katarina Johnson-Thompson and eight other stars pull out of Commonwealth Games in major blow

Katarina Johnson-Thompson is one of several stars to pull out of this summer's Commonwealth Games in Glasgow with problems mounting for the troubled event

View 2 Images Katarina Johnson-Thompson won't be at the 2026 Commonwealth Games (Image: Getty Images)

Katarina Johnson-Thompson is among nine England stars to pull out of this summer's Commonwealth Games. The event has been plagued with problems in the build-up.

‌



The original hosts, Victoria, Australia, effectively paid AUS$380million (£199m) to pull out in July 2023 because it feared losses running into the billions. Glasgow then stepped in to host a cheaper and stripped-back event, with only 10 sports compared to 19 in Birmingham four years ago.

‌



Glasgow also hosted the Games in 2014 and was therefore in a position to offer a solution of a condensed format using existing venues to minimise taxpayer costs. But now some of the competition's leading athletes have withdrawn.

‌



Johnson-Thompson and Dina Asher-Smith are among the latest big names to pull out. The duo are two of nine members of the England athletics team to withdraw on the day of the opening ceremony - dealing a major blow to competition organisers.

Fellow Olympic medallists Matthew Hudson-Smith and Daryll Neita have also announced their withdrawals alongside Amber Anning, Zac Sneddon, Anna Purchase, Elliot Giles and Jona Efoloko.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Liverpool-born Johnson-Thompson had been expected to target a hat-trick of Commonwealth Games titles, having previously won gold in both the Gold Coast and Birmingham editions.

But the 33-year-old is still recovering from an injury ‌and has chosen to prioritise next month's European Championships in Birmingham.

View 2 Images Katarina Johnson-Thompson will not defend her Commonwealth Games heptathlon title

‌



Posting on Instagram, she said: "I'm gutted to have to pull out of ⁠this year's Commonwealth Games. I was so looking forward to competing on home soil and having the chance to defend my Commonwealth title!

"Although the injury I picked up earlier this season has improved, I haven't been able to get back to the level I need to compete at my best. After discussing it with my team, we've made the difficult decision to ‌focus ⁠on giving myself the best chance of being ready for the European Championships, so working very hard to be there later this season.

"Missing a championship is never easy, but I know it's the right ⁠decision. I can't wait to be back competing again soon."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

The hectic schedule has posed a quandary for several leading athletes including Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson, who decided not to compete at the Glasgow Games.

International stars who have previously pulled out of the Games include multiple Olympic swimming medallists Kaylee McKeown and Summer McIntosh of Australia and Canada, respectively, and Hodgkinson's 800m rival, Mary Moraa of Kenya.

Article continues below

Away from the athletics track, triple Olympic gymnastics champion Max Whitlock was forced to call time on his comeback bid earlier this month due to injury.

The ⁠Commonwealth Games will run from Thursday to August 2, while the European Athletics Championships are scheduled for August 10-16.

Sports.title: Man Utd XI from last Rosenborg friendly with six axed and two more potential transfers
Sports.content:
Man Utd XI from last Rosenborg friendly with six axed and two more potential transfers

A lot has changed since Manchester United last met Rosenborg

View 2 Images Less than half of the starters from Manchester United's previous trip to Rosenborg still play for the club (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United are due to take on Rosenborg this week, some two years on from their last meeting. Those two years have been incredibly eventful, though, with the Premier League club undergoing a huge upheaval - and not just with the playing staff.

‌



Erik ten Hag was still United's manager when that match in Trondheim took place. He had just led the Red Devils to FA Cup glory but pre-season got off to a tough start when Noah Holm scored the winner in Trondheim.

‌



Ten Hag was gone just months later with Ruben Amorim taking his place. However, the Portuguese coach only lasted 14 months in the hotseat before his January 2026 exit, meaning Michael Carrick is in charge for the latest trip to Norway.

‌



Changes in the dugout have also been accompanied by an overhaul of the playing staff. Six of the 11 players who started the last Rosenborg game have since left or retired, while two more could yet leave Old Trafford before the current window is up.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Bruno Fernandes commits future to Manchester United despite new contract wait READ MORE :

Man Utd release new 2026/27 away kit with striking blue design READ MORE :

Radek Vitek started in goal that day and is the sole survivor of the back five still on the books at Old Trafford. The Czech started behind centre-back Jonny Evans - now retired and part of Carrick's coaching staff - and three other defenders now playing elsewhere.

‌



Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Will Fish both left the following month and could end up facing one another in the Championship before too long. Wan-Bissaka's West Ham are newly relegated to the second tier while Fish's Cardiff won promotion last season.

The defence was rounded out by academy graduate Sam Murray, who left for Carlisle in 2025 and is now looking for a new club again. As for Vitek, a promise of first team football could tempt him away.

View 2 Images Aaron Wan-Bissaka left United just a month after the friendly in Norway (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



"At the moment, I am still here, but we will see. I hope so," he said after featuring against Wrexham in United's first friendly of the summer. "I hope there will be some interest. I think you will know when things are more concrete."

Further forward, Casemiro gave United two more years but left in the summer of 2026. The Brazilian is now at Inter Miami, with a strong end to last season not enough to keep him around.

He played in midfield with Mason Mount and Hannibal Mejbri that day. While Mount is still a United player, impressing against Wrexham, Hannibal is long gone.

‌



The Tunisian international sealed a permanent move to Burnley in August 2024 and remains at Turf Moor to this day. He helped the Clarets win promotion to the Premier League but they dropped straight back down last term.

Pre-season regularly gives clubs the opportunity to blood younger talent, particularly while waiting for international players to return from major tournaments. Ethan Williams and Ethan Wheatley are both still at United, having started that Rosenborg game, as are some of the youngsters who came off the bench in Trondheim.

Completing the front three was Marcus Rashford, who had surprisingly been overlooked by Gareth Southgate for England's Euro 2024 squad. The forward spent the 2025/26 season on loan at Barcelona but his future is up in the air again after the Catalan club opted against triggering a buy option, and manager Carrick will have a decision to make on the academy graduate.

Sports.title: Christos Tzolis: How Arsenal's new £34m signing went from Norwich flop to Champions League star
Sports.content:
It says everything about the evolution of Christos Tzolis that Arsenal's newest signing accrued more goal contributions last year than he made league appearances across an ill-fated spell at Norwich City.

The reason Tzolis will play for the newly minted Premier League champions is because, at 24, he is now every inch the clinical, cold-blooded attacker that Europe's elite believed he would become back when he was a teenager. Barcelona were among his illustrious courters back then as heavyweights flocked to observe a prodigious talent. But it was Norwich, rather than Barcelona, who clinched the youngster's sought-after signature.

The Tzolis hype train was already in full flow when the formalities of his £8.8million transfer from PAOK was confirmed back in the summer of 2021. At 21, Tzolis was already a full Greece international; for a Norwich side who were back in the big-time after romping to the Championship title under Daniel Farke, the winger's capture had all the hallmarks of a transfer coup.

And yet, things deteriorated rapidly. After scoring twice in a 6-0 win over Bournemouth in the Carabao Cup on his debut, Tzolis soon fell out of favour. By early November, Tzolis had seen the manager who signed him sacked by the club, just hours after recording Norwich's first league win of the season.

‌



Dean Smith's appointment as Farke's successor proved to be the catalyst for the change of shape which effectively killed Tzolis' Norwich career.

Alex Scott transfer twist as Bournemouth star ‘keen’ on rivals amid Arsenal and Man Utd race READ MORE :

Arsenal respond to Morgan Rogers transfer snub as £34m signing flies in for medical READ MORE :

“It was the hardest year of my career,” Arsenal's newest attacker conceded to Het Nieuwsblad back in 2024. “The first time I didn’t play with the first team, but with the second [reserves], I was very disappointed. That was the lowest point of my career.

“My agent and my family had to convince me not to give up. And life off the pitch wasn’t easy back then.”

In total, Tzolis made just 27 appearances for Norwich before leaving the club permanently in the summer of 2024. The first of two loan spells designed to resurrect his career, with FC Twente, fell flat due to a knee injury. It was in the second tier of German football with Fortuna Dusseldorf that the youngster finally rediscovered his killer instinct, plundering more than 20 goals.

‌



From there, he never looked back. Unsurprisingly, Dusseldorf triggered their option to sign him permanently for just £3m. But it was Tzolis' next move which put the teen prodigy back on the path to superstardom.

Club Brugge swooped in to offer Dusseldorf the chance to effectively double their money instantly. They accepted and, in Belgium, Tzolis has flourished, accumulating more than 20 goals in successive seasons. Not only did he score 22 times last term, he registered a staggering 29 assists to break out as one of the biggest stars in the Belgian Pro League.

View 3 Images Christos Tzolis has transformed into a different player with Club Brugge (Image: JASPER JACOBS, BELGA MAG/AFP via Getty Images)

Tzolis returns to these shores not only hardened by the challenges of his stint in Norfolk, but brimming with confidence. Deadly with his right-foot, he has thrived in a left-sided attacking role and is viewed as the successor to the revered Leandro Trossard, who completed a move to Besiktas last week.

‌



Speaking to The Telegraph, Norwich's sporting director at the time Tzolis was signed, Stuart Webber, cites the physicality of the Premier League as one of the reasons behind the young attacker's failure to live up to expectations. “He was very young, coming into the hardest league in the world where the physicality is off the charts,” said Webber.

“It didn’t work out because we [Norwich] were a struggling team in an unforgiving division. Attacking players don’t get 100 touches of the ball when they are playing for Norwich. If he’d been at an Arsenal he would have probably been successful straight away.”

Tzolis returns to the Premier League a different beast. Naturally, he has grown physically and looks more robust than the twinkle-eyed teenager who was swatted aside both figuratively and literally at Norwich. The numbers he has put up consistently elsewhere in Europe, albeit at a level which is not elite, are eye-catching. His previous experience, although chastening, should give him some form of advantage when it comes to adapting to the rigours of Premier League life this time around.

“I’m a direct player, I go for goals or assists,” Tzolis told Arsenal’s website. “That’s my point of view as an attacker, as a winger. I’m always hungry to score or to give the final pass to my teammates. And I can say I work hard for the team, also in the defensive part.”

‌



View 3 Images Christos Tzolis struggled previously in the Premier League for Norwich City (Image: Ryan Pierse)

Arsenal went into the summer with designs on levelling up their attack, particularly on the left side. A deal for Morgan Rogers is now off the table, and Tzolis will not be the only acquisition in that area. Whereas at Tzolis organically became the main man at Brugge, his role at Arsenal will be significantly different.

There is, of course, the risk that Tzolis' exceptional record in Belgium does not translate to the Premier League. Even with the additional experience and nous under his belt.

In a transfer market where the Premier League's heavyweights have focused on domestic signings for inflated transfer fees this summer, the signing of Tzolis is somewhat of an outlier.

‌



But considering the transfer fee, the prospective upsides to the deal and the fact Arsenal are still after a ceiling-raiser signing for the left wing berth, you can see why signing Tzolis is a risk they feel is worth taking.

Sports.title: BHA freezes activity of leading syndicate after members complain they’ve not been paid
Sports.content:
BHA freezes activity of leading syndicate after members complain they’ve not been paid

No entries or declarations will be allowed for Deva Racing whose flagship horse Imperial Emperor has won nearly £1.5 million in prize-money

View 4 Images Imperial Emperor is a star for Deva Racing run by Ryan Tongue (inset)

The BHA has put a stop to entries and declarations for horses owned by a popular racing syndicate after members complained they had not been paid.

‌



The Deva Racing Syndicate has a dozen horses in training in stables in Britain, the US and Dubai, managed by Ryan Tongue, who as a teenager served tea to 20-champion jockey Sir AP McCoy when he worked in the Worcester weighing room.

‌



Tongue, 30, has worked in a number of roles in racing, briefly as a jockey and then as a racing manager when he was involved in the purchase of dual Grand National winner I Am Maximus for the late owner Michael Grech.

‌



Seven years ago he took over Deva Racing, whose flagship horse Imperial Emperor brought the syndicate to national attention through his exploits in Dubai.

Trawlerman vs Scandinavia Goodwood Cup rematch set after Gold Cup thriller READ MORE :

The gelding, who was bought from Godolphin for £63,000 and put into training with local champion trainer Bhupat Seemar, has been transformed into a dirt performer.

He has won five of his eight starts for Seemar and earned a start in the last two runnings of the Dubai World Cup, one of the world’s richest races.

‌



View 4 Images Deva Racing members on the podium in Dubai (Image: Dubai Racing Club)

After two victories, including at Group 1 level during the latest carnival and a fourth place in the World Cup, his winnings have risen to nearly £1.5 million.

However attempts by syndicate members to secure their share of the prize-money from his latest campaign have been unsuccessful and as a result the problems have been brought to the attention of the BHA.

‌



One of the members, Tom Walton from Leeds, who works for a Manchester law firm, told Mirror Racing: “We have uncovered the overselling of shares and ultimately Ryan has kept prize-money.

View 4 Images Imperial Emperor has won nearly £1.5 million (Image: Dubai Racing Club)

“I got paid roughly £7,000 last year but I do know of one syndicate member who got nothing. We’ve not received any prize-money from this season when the horse won £760,000.

‌



“The last response I had from Ryan was on June 19 which said he wouldn’t be speaking to me, only to another member Mark. Ryan then blocked me and Mark is getting no response too.

“The BHA gave him a deadline and he told them he would endeavour to pay within 60 days but he was currently experiencing ill-health.”

In April, Walton discovered that Imperial Emperor had been entered in an online auction in Dubai without his knowledge. The gelding was withdrawn from the sale and the 20 original owning members subsequently completed a deal to buy the horse.

‌



View 4 Images Bhupat Seemar, the trainer of Imperial Emperor (Image: YouTube)

Walton said: “I wouldn’t want this experience to put anyone off getting involved in racing. Ryan and Deva are certainly outliers. The shining light is we’ve still got the horse and we can run him next season.

“I’ve kind of written the money off but what I want is to make sure that Ryan and Deva don’t have any involvement in racing again.

Article continues below

“I am presently a part owner in a syndicate run by My Future Champion. They’re a great outfit and I don’t want this experience to stain the whole syndicate world when there’s one like them around.”

A spokesperson for the BHA said “We can confirm that the BHA has put a stop on entries and declarations being made for Deva Racing Syndicate horses trained in Britain. We encourage any concerned syndicate members to contact the BHA on intel@britishhorseracing.com. We will be making no further comment regarding this matter at this time.”

Ryan Tongue has been approached for comment.

Sports.title: Newsboy’s horseracing tips for Friday’s six meetings, including Ascot Nap
Sports.content:
Newsboy’s horseracing tips for Friday’s six meetings, including Ascot Nap

Newsboy fancies his Nap, Paradise Walk, to win at Ascot and also hopes Imperial Cult can score at Sandown and complete his Daily Double

View 2 Images Ascot hosts a six-race Flat meeting on Friday when Newsboy’s nap, Paradise Walk, is fancied to win the finale (5.12) (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

PARADISE WALK looks ripe for a hat-trick in the Sodexo Live! Fillies' Handicap (5.12) at Ascot on Friday afternoon. The Ralph Beckett-trained daughter of Starman qualified for a British Horseracing Authority handicap mark of 78 on the back of second placings at Chelmsford City and Southwell and Wolverhampton. Fitted with blinkers, Paradise Walk didn’t shine on her debut in the sphere when ninth to Cinque Verde on the first day of Newmarket’s Guineas Festival at the beginning of May. But Paradise Walk took a big step forward to gain a first career success from three rivals in a six-furlong handicap at Windsor next time, beating Space Party by three-quarters of a length. And my selection followed up back at five when accounting for Secret Mistral at Nottingham last time out. The assessor’s latest recalculation means that Hector Crouch’s partner must compete from a rating of 80 after a 4lb rise. But there is more to come and a third straight win is on the cards.

‌



View 2 Images Ascot hosts a six-race Flat meeting on Friday when Newsboy’s nap, Paradise Walk, is fancied to win the finale (5.12) (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

‌



At Sandown, IMPERIAL CULT and Jack Callan are expected to prove a potent combination in the Close Brothers Asset Finance Apprentice Handicap (5.15). After all-weather successes at Lingfield and Kempton Park, George Baker’s seven-year-old stumbled leaving the stalls in search of the hat-trick at Epsom but still rattled home to be beaten less than a length in fourth behind Super Hit. Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
