LAGOS — The Pentecostal Fellowship of Nigeria (PFN) has urged President Bola Tinubu not to assent to the anti-preaching and hawking bill currently before the National Assembly, describing it as unnecessary and unrelated to the country’s pressing challenges.

The Christian body said the proposed legislation was not among the urgent issues requiring government attention, insisting that Nigeria’s major problems bordered on insecurity, hunger and economic hardship.

Speaking with journalists in Lagos after the meeting of its National Executive Council, PFN National Secretary, Bishop David Bakare, described the bill as a needless measure targeted at Christians.

Bakare said Nigeria’s challenge was not a lack of laws but poor enforcement of existing ones.

“Many laws already exist in Nigeria which, if properly enforced, can bring sanity to different aspects of our national life. Our concern is that this law is not the urgent need of Nigerians at this time,” he said.

He argued that the country had more critical issues demanding attention, including insecurity and hardship, adding that the proposed legislation would not provide solutions to the challenges facing citizens.

The PFN secretary questioned the rationale behind classifying preaching in commercial vehicles as a traffic offence, saying legislators should have consulted more widely before considering such a measure.

“We cannot understand how this has become a traffic offence in any form. There are other issues that can be considered traffic offences in Nigeria that have not been addressed,” he said.

Bakare also raised concerns over the legislative process surrounding the bill, saying the organisation was unaware of its progress in the House of Representatives after its passage by the Senate.

He warned that religious matters required careful handling in Nigeria because of their sensitivity, stressing that the bill could create unnecessary tension between religious groups and the government.

“Christians in Nigeria consider that law as being against the church. It is deliberately organised to stir up the church against the state,” he said.

He appealed to President Tinubu to withhold assent and return the bill for wider public consultation involving relevant stakeholders.

“Let the public debate it. Invite the relevant people who are directly affected by such laws to come and discuss it,” Bakare added.

The PFN maintained that the proposed law did not address the country’s core challenges and should not be prioritised at this time.

World.title: Osun Election: I didn’t own house while serving as Osun governor — Aregbesola
World.content:
By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo

OSOGBO — National Secretary of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Rauf Aregbesola, has claimed that he did not own a personal house throughout his eight years as governor of Osun State.

Aregbesola made the claim while addressing supporters in a video that circulated online on Thursday.

The former governor said he lived in a friend’s house in the Amuta area of Ilesa during his tenure, challenging anyone with contrary information to prove otherwise.

“I’m the first governor in Nigeria to govern a state for eight years without owning a house of my own. I stayed in my friend’s house for eight years as governor in my fatherland. Whoever says what I’m saying is not true should come out and show me the house I own,” he said.

Aregbesola governed Osun State from 2010 to 2018 before serving as Minister of Interior under former President Muhammadu Buhari.

He is currently leading the ADC governorship campaign in Osun State, following the grand opening of the party’s campaign in Ile-Ife on Tuesday.

World.title: Igboho vows to flush out bandits from Kwara forests
World.content:
Launches Iru Ekun Security Network, says outfit will support security agencies

By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin

ILORIN — Yoruba Nation activist, Sunday Adeyemo, popularly known as Sunday Igboho, has vowed that his Iru Ekun Security Network will reclaim forests in Kwara State from bandits and other criminal elements.

Igboho made the declaration on Thursday in Ilorin during the launch of the security outfit at Igbomina House, stressing that criminals would no longer be allowed to use the state’s forests as hideouts for violent activities.

He said the initiative was established to complement the efforts of government and conventional security agencies in tackling kidnapping, banditry and other security challenges affecting communities across the state.

Igboho also dismissed reports that Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq was opposed to his visit to Kwara, saying he believed the governor shared residents’ concerns over rising cases of insecurity.

“I should have arrived in Ilorin much earlier, but there were rumours that the governor did not approve of my visit. I found that difficult to believe because I know Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq would not make such a decision,” he said.

The activist commended the Kwara State Commissioner of Police, Adekimi Ojo, for his professionalism and support during previous security operations, particularly rescue efforts around forests linking Oyo and Kwara states.

According to him, operatives of the Iru Ekun Security Network would begin security operations in Babanla and revisit Eruku, two communities he identified as being affected by insecurity.

“The presence of the Iru Ekun Security Network in Kwara has already unsettled the criminals. We are heading to Babanla, which many people now describe as a stronghold of bandits,” he said.

Igboho stressed that the outfit was not created to replace the police, military or other security agencies, but to strengthen ongoing efforts to restore peace.

“Our mission in Kwara is to complement the efforts of government and security agencies. We must work hand in hand with the police, the military and other security agencies. If we unite, we can drastically reduce kidnapping, banditry and every other form of terrorism,” he said.

He alleged that criminal activities persist partly because of support from some local collaborators, urging residents, especially youths, to provide useful information to security agencies.

Igboho also dismissed claims that the security network was established to target any ethnic group, insisting that its focus was on criminals irrespective of their background.

“We have no problem with innocent Fulani people or any other ethnic group. Our fight is against criminals, regardless of where they come from. We are all Nigerians,” he said.

He advised residents not to take the law into their own hands but to report suspected criminals to security agencies, adding that individuals carrying weapons in forests and threatening communities should be treated as security risks.

Igboho attributed the establishment of the Iru Ekun Security Network to President Bola Tinubu, praying for the President’s continued good health and successful tenure.

He added that the outfit had been directed to collaborate with the Nigeria Police Force and other recognised security agencies in its operations across Kwara State.

World.title: Lawan applauds Tinubu’s expansion of army to 12 Divisions
World.content:
Lawan

Commends recruitment of 28,000 personnel, says move will improve response to security threats

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — Former Senate President and Chairman of the Senate Committee on Defence, Senator Ahmad Lawan (APC, Yobe North), has commended President Bola Tinubu for expanding the Nigerian Army to 12 divisions and approving the recruitment of 28,000 young Nigerians into the military.

Lawan, in a statement he personally signed on Wednesday, described the decision as a strategic move that would strengthen Nigeria’s security architecture and enhance the military’s capacity to respond to emerging threats.

He said the creation of additional divisions would reduce response time to security challenges, particularly in ungoverned spaces, adding that a stronger military structure would help accelerate efforts to end insurgency and other security threats.

Lawan said, “The asymmetric nature of modern warfare requires not just superior firepower, but superior manpower, strategic spread and operational agility. With this expansion, the Commander-in-Chief has demonstrated that he is not just a listening leader, but a thinking leader.”

According to him, the recruitment of 28,000 young Nigerians into the Army would strengthen national defence while creating employment opportunities for youths and reducing their vulnerability to crime and extremism.

He added that the reforms in the nation’s security sector would contribute to the success of the Renewed Hope Agenda of the Tinubu administration, stressing that efforts to secure the country must be sustained.

“More robust order of battle means a faster and more decisive end to the remnants of insurgency that have troubled our peace,” Lawan said.

He prayed for the success of the Nigerian Armed Forces and the continued peace and stability of the country.

World.title: Nigerian onion traders seek Ghana’s intervention over detention of trucks
World.content:
Onions

By Cynthia Alo

The Regional Observatory of Onion in West and Central Africa, ORO/WCA, has appealed to the Government of Ghana to urgently intervene in the continued detention of five trucks loaded with Nigerian onions at Kotoku Market, warning that the development is causing heavy losses on farmers, exporters and traders.

In a statement signed by its President, Aliyu Isah, who is also the National President of the National Onion Producers, Processors and Marketers Association of Nigeria (NOPPMAN), ORO said some Ghanaian onion traders had prevented the trucks from offloading their consignments since Tuesday.

The regional body said the prolonged delay is particularly damaging because onions are highly perishable commodities.

“If this situation persists, the quality of the produce will continue to deteriorate, leading to avoidable economic losses for farmers, traders and businesses that depend on cross-border trade,” the statement said.

ORO disclosed that several diplomatic efforts had been made to resolve the impasse, including engagements with trader associations in Ghana and interventions by the ECOWAS Trade Directorate through the trade ministries of both countries, but the matter remains unresolved.

The organisation noted that Ghanaian onion traders operating in Nigeria conduct their businesses freely without discrimination, urging Ghanaian authorities to extend the same treatment to Nigerian traders.

Isah said the continued obstruction of legitimate onion trade contradicts the objectives of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which promote the free movement of goods and regional economic integration.

ORO therefore called on the Ghanaian government to facilitate the immediate release of the trucks and restore the smooth flow of agricultural trade between both countries.

Speaking further on the issue exclusively to Vanguard, Isah revealed that about five trucks have remained stranded despite interventions by the Nigerian Ministry of Trade, the Ghanaian Ministry of Trade and ECOWAS.

“Approximately five trucks that were detained from Tuesday till today. We have reported the issue to the relevant authorities. The Nigerian Ministry of Trade are doing their best, ECOWAS are aware, and even the Ghana Ministry of Trade are working to resolve it,” he said.

He alleged that a group of traders in Ghana was attempting to dominate the onion market.

“The onion is produced mainly in Nigeria and Niger Republic and consumed across West Africa. When Ghanaian traders come to Nigeria, they buy freely without discrimination. But when we go to Ghana, they keep introducing different rules, which is very bad.

“We want to solve the issue amicably. As president of the regional body, I have to remain neutral because ORO represents all member countries. We just pray that this time government will bring everybody to the table and resolve the matter,” Isah added.

ORO reaffirmed its commitment to dialogue, expressing hope that the dispute would be resolved quickly to preserve the longstanding trade relationship between Nigeria and Ghana and strengthen regional agricultural trade.

World.title: Nasarawa lawmaker raises alarm over killing of 32 persons in constituency
World.content:
By Edwin Philip, Lafia

A member of the Nasarawa State House of Assembly representing Udege/Loko Constituency, Hon. Onarigu Onah Kana, has raised the alarm over renewed violence in his constituency, alleging that at least 32 people have been killed in the last three months.

Speaking under a matter of public importance on the floor of the House, Kana said the persistent attacks had left residents living in fear and disrupted farming and other economic activities in several communities.

According to him, the crisis, which began on April 3, 2026, in Odeni Gida Electoral Ward of Nasarawa Local Government Area, has resulted in loss of lives, injuries, displacement of residents and destruction of property.

He alleged that over 200 residents had been displaced from their homes, while houses, vehicles, motorcycles, foodstuffs, farmlands and other valuables worth millions of naira had been destroyed.

Kana also claimed that communities including Angwan Mada, Apura Adagba, Udege Kasa, Akyewa and Angwan Ogiri had been affected by the violence.

“The people can no longer sleep with their two eyes closed. They are afraid to go to their farms, while crops are being destroyed by cattle,” he said.

The lawmaker further alleged that two more persons were killed in Akum Electoral Ward on June 25 and July 9, 2026, warning that the violence could spread to neighbouring communities if urgent action was not taken.

He urged the House to condemn the attacks and call on security agencies to immediately deploy personnel to the affected communities to restore peace and protect lives and property.

Kana also called on the Nasarawa State Emergency Management Agency (NASEMA) and the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) to provide relief materials, including food, medical supplies and temporary shelter, to displaced victims.

In addition, he urged the House Committee on Security and Special Duties to investigate the remote causes of the crisis and report back to the Assembly.

Responding, Speaker of the House, Dr. Danladi Jatau, described the renewed attacks as unfortunate and called on Governor Abdullahi Sule to direct the Commissioner of Police to deploy more personnel to Udege and other affected communities.

He also urged traditional rulers and community leaders to establish peace and reconciliation committees in their domains to promote peaceful coexistence.

Jatau further appealed to the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) to deploy personnel to the affected areas to strengthen security.

The Speaker directed the Clerk of the House to communicate the Assembly’s resolutions to Governor Sule for necessary action.

Several lawmakers, including Hon. Ibrahim Abdullahi Sa’ad, Hon. Esson Mairiga, Hon. Hudu A. Hudu, Hon. Musa Ibrahim Abubakar, Hon. Solomon Yakubu Akwashiki and Hon. Ibrahim Peter Akwe, supported the motion and called for increased deployment of security personnel to communities facing similar security challenges across the state.

World.title: Collapsed Benin–Sapele–Warri Road: End cycle of palliative repairs, Ugolor urges Oborevwori
World.content:
Gov. Oborevwori

Demands cost of governor’s ordered emergency repairs

By Egufe Yafugborhi

ASABA — Civil society leader, Rev. David Ugolor, has urged Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, to engage the Federal Government and neighbouring Edo State to end decades of temporary repairs on the collapsed Benin–Sapele–Warri Road and commit to its full reconstruction.

In an open letter to the governor published in the July 2026 edition of his accountability advocacy report, The Common Good Letter, Ugolor said palliative repairs on the Oghara–Mosogar section of the road, though commendable, would not end the hardship faced by commuters.

He made the call on Thursday while commending Governor Oborevwori for ordering immediate repairs after the failed Oghara–Mosogar stretch left motorists stranded for days, disrupted the movement of goods and exposed travellers to security risks.

According to Ugolor, “While this intervention is welcomed, it must also be stated that palliative repairs cannot solve a structural failure of national infrastructure.

“Without comprehensive reconstruction, many of these repaired sections may deteriorate again within a short period, resulting in another cycle of emergency interventions funded by taxpayers. This is neither economically prudent nor sustainable.”

He described the Benin–Sapele–Warri Road as one of Nigeria’s most strategic highways and a major economic gateway to the Niger Delta, lamenting that it has suffered years of neglect despite substantial federal allocations to the Federal Ministry of Works and the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC).

Ugolor blamed corruption, weak contract management and poor accountability for the road’s deterioration, saying the impact on residents and road users had been severe.

“Many lives have been lost in avoidable road accidents. Businesses have suffered heavy economic losses. Farmers struggle to transport their produce, while patients experience delays in accessing healthcare.

“More alarming is the growing insecurity. The deplorable condition of the road has created opportunities for kidnappers and other criminal elements who prey on stranded motorists,” he said.

The activist also urged the Delta State Government to make public details of the palliative repair contract, including the contract sum, scope of work, implementation timeline, procurement process and monitoring mechanisms.

“Providing this information is not merely an administrative exercise. It is a demonstration of good governance and respect for the citizens whose taxes fund public infrastructure,” Ugolor said.

He further called on Governor Oborevwori to lead a regional advocacy with Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, other Niger Delta governors, members of the National Assembly and key stakeholders to press for urgent federal intervention on the East-West Road.

Specifically, Ugolor urged the Federal Government to declare a state of emergency on the East-West Road, provide dedicated funding for its complete reconstruction, publish details of all contracts and project milestones, and establish an independent monitoring mechanism involving civil society organisations and host communities.

“The East-West Road is not merely another highway. It is a national economic corridor that connects people, commerce, industries and critical oil and gas infrastructure.

“Its continued deterioration undermines economic growth, threatens public safety and weakens national development.

“The lives already lost cannot be restored. But many more can still be saved. The people of Delta, Edo and the entire Niger Delta deserve a safe, modern and durable East-West Road, not another cycle of temporary repairs,” he said.

World.title: NDIC promotes financial literacy, deposit protection in Ebonyi
World.content:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) has organised a financial literacy campaign for students in Ebonyi State to enhance their knowledge of personal finance and create awareness about the protection of bank deposits.

The awareness programme was held for staff and students of Urban Model Secondary School, Abakaliki, as part of activities marking the 2026 Global Money Week.

Speaking at the event, the Principal Manager, Communication and Public Affairs, NDIC, Mr. Toke Afolayan, said the initiative was aimed at promoting financial literacy among young Nigerians while supporting stability in the banking sector.

Afolayan said the programme, themed “Small Money Talks,” provided an opportunity for the corporation to educate students on its core mandates, including protecting depositors and promoting stability in the banking system.

He explained that the financial literacy campaign was designed to equip young people with the knowledge and skills needed to make sound financial decisions, including saving, investing and managing money responsibly.

According to him, “Financial literacy is about acquiring the skills to make sound financial decisions. If you acquire what we describe as financial literacy, you should be able to know which bank to keep your money in instead of keeping it at home. Once you acquire the right skills, such decisions will no longer be difficult.”

He urged the students to cultivate what he described as “smart spending habits” by spending prudently, prioritising their needs and avoiding unnecessary debt.

Also speaking, a Senior Manager at the NDIC, Shehu Umar-Mohammed, said the corporation provides insurance cover for depositors in licensed banks and other financial institutions in Nigeria, while also collaborating with the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to facilitate mergers and acquisitions where necessary.

He assured participants that the establishment of the NDIC had strengthened confidence in the banking system by protecting depositors against the loss of insured funds.

The Ebonyi State Commissioner for Education, Dr. Donatus Ilang, represented by Mr. Igwe Nwuruku, and the Principal of Urban Model Secondary School, Abakaliki, Mr. Paul Odigbo, commended the NDIC for extending the financial literacy campaign to students in the state.

World.title: Ex-President Obasanjo Clashes with Osoba over Alleged Claims of 2003 Elections Deceit
World.content:
James Sowole in Abeokuta





Former President Olusegun Obasanjo, yesterday, replied to claims by former Ogun State governor, Aremo Olusegun Osoba, that he deceived leaders of the Alliance for Democracy (AD) during the political realignments preceding the 2003 General Election.

Obasanjo declared that he neither misled nor deceived anyone in processes that led to the Election but he only held wide consultations to consolidate on the success of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

Obasanjo’s strongly worded and lengthy letter dated July 23, 2026, was entitled: “Reply to Your Inaccurate Posture: ‘How Obasanjo Deceived Us in 2003’.

He described Osoba’s account, published in The Legal Observer on July 20, as “farfetched” and riddled with inaccuracies, omissions and misconceptions.

The former President took particular exception to Osoba’s allegation that he deceived Yoruba political leaders, insisting that his political engagements had always been guided by openness and national interest.

He said, “I take strong and serious objection to your calling me a deceiver because I deceived nobody. I always presented my case and all issues as I had them and as I understood them, no matter whose ox is gored.”

Obasanjo argued that several political developments preceding his emergence as President in 1999 were unknown to Osoba because they were handled by senior leaders of Afenifere and the AD.

He disclosed that after his release from prison, several groups from across the country urged him to contest for the presidency, including delegations led by Lawan Katsina, the late Chief S.M. Afolabi and Chief Martins Kuye.

According to him, those consultations informed his eventual decision to join the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) after extensive consultations with political leaders across the South-West, North and South-East.

Recalling his engagements with the late Afenifere leader, Chief Abraham Adesanya, Obasanjo said despite being repeatedly told that Yoruba people would not vote for him, he continued to maintain cordial relations with the elder statesman.

“There was no time I called on Papa Adesanya that I was not well entertained. Yet Papa stood on no vote for me, and I stood on my respect and what was due to him,” he stated.

The former President defended his decision to invite the AD into what he described as a broad-based national government after winning the presidency, saying it was motivated by a desire to promote national unity rather than political weakness.

“Bringing PDP and AD to join me for a sort of national government was not out of weakness; rather, it was out of strength and for the unity and progress of the country.”

Obasanjo also rejected Osoba’s account of events surrounding the attempted impeachment of then Speaker of the House of Representatives, Ghali Na’Abba, alleging instead that the impeachment plot originated from within his own administration.

He claimed that his then Vice-President had encouraged the move while simultaneously pursuing his own presidential ambition.

“The game continued to be played on with me treating it with contempt as I had committed no impeachable offence,” he wrote.

On the 2003 elections, Obasanjo disputed Osoba’s suggestion that the defeat of AD governors resulted from political manipulation by the Presidency.

Instead, he maintained that the electoral outcome reflected the political realities at the time.

“Your loss or defeat in 2003 was genuine in all the six states except the one where the figures were successfully and murderously changed,” he asserted.

World.title: Nigeria Losing Billions To ‘Hidden Hunger’ as Health Experts Demand Compulsory Fortification of Seasoning Cubes
World.content:
Mary Nnah





A nutrition emergency most Nigerians cannot see is quietly eroding the country’s growth, with experts warning that widespread gaps in folate and vitamin B12 are behind preventable birth defects, stunted brain development, poor school performance and a less productive workforce.

Faced with the scale of the problem, nutrition specialists are calling on the federal government to make it compulsory for bouillon cubes to be fortified with folic acid and vitamin B12, describing the move as one of the cheapest and fastest ways to improve public health and protect the nation’s human capital.

The push comes at a time when Nigeria records roughly 7.5 million births each year. Buried in that figure are about 11,000 infants born annually with neural tube defects, devastating conditions of the brain and spine that research links directly to folate deficiency.

Studies show that getting enough folic acid before conception and in early pregnancy can cut the risk of these defects by up to 70 percent.

The fallout goes well beyond hospital wards. Children born with preventable neural tube defects often live with lifelong medical needs, multiple surgeries, therapy and special care.

The burden lands on families, on an already stretched health system, and on the economy through lost schooling, weaker job output and wasted potential.

“If Nigeria is serious about growth and building human capital, then hidden hunger has to be treated as a national priority. A healthy population drives a productive economy,” experts said.

In Nigeria, neural tube defects rank as the second most common congenital neurological condition. They include spina bifida where the spine fails to close properly, anencephaly where major parts of the brain do not develop and is usually fatal, and encephalocele where brain tissue pushes through an opening in the skull.

While some children survive with intensive support, many die shortly after birth or grow up with disabilities that leave families emotionally and financially drained.

Doctors say a large number of these cases could be avoided if women had enough folic acid before they conceive and in the first month of pregnancy, a window when most do not even know they are pregnant.

That reality is driving renewed calls for mandatory fortification of bouillon cubes, a seasoning found in nearly every Nigerian kitchen across income levels and regions.

Unlike daily supplements that require clinic access and consistent use, fortified bouillon would deliver folic acid and B12 through meals people already cook every day.

Dr. Jamila Lawal, a nutritionist and public health expert, said the approach has worked elsewhere.

“Why not fortify what people already eat? We fortify flour with vitamin A and nobody questions it.

Bouillon is part of our daily cooking. It reaches almost every home and it is the right channel to get folic acid to women, especially before and during pregnancy,” Lawal said.

She noted that depending only on tablets has fallen short because many women start too late or do not keep up with them.

“Fortification is not a replacement for supplements. It fills the gap by putting nutrients into the food we eat every day,” she added.

Olusola Malomo, Assistant Director of Dietetics at Lagos State Health Service Commission, General Hospital Badagry, said fortification could make a real dent in neural tube defects but only with strong regulation.

“If the goal is to reduce these birth defects, then it is a welcome step. Government must ensure the exact amount of folic acid goes into the cubes, not too low and not excessive. Agencies also have to confirm that companies are actually adding the stated vitamins and not just flavor,” Malomo said.

He urged producers to carry out proper scientific tests before rollout and called for mass public education on taking folic acid before conception and through the first eight weeks of pregnancy.

He also suggested creating lower-sodium fortified cubes aimed specifically at women planning pregnancy and those already pregnant.

Evidence from the region backs the idea. A major Condiment Micronutrient Innovation Trial in Ghana involving over 2,000 women and children showed that bouillon fortified with folic acid and vitamin B12 raised blood levels of both nutrients significantly.

Researchers concluded that bouillon can deliver key micronutrients at scale across West Africa, where it is used in almost every household.

Nigeria set voluntary fortification guidelines for bouillon in September 2024, permitting the addition of folic acid, vitamin B12, iron, zinc and iodine.

Experts, however, say voluntary compliance has moved too slowly to create nationwide change. Current estimates show more than 40 percent of women of reproductive age in Nigeria do not get enough folate, while B12 deficiency is common in low-income homes with little access to animal-based foods.

For nutrition advocates, the question is no longer if fortification works, but whether leaders will act. As Nigeria works to meet 2030 global nutrition goals and unlock its demographic potential, they argue that compulsory bouillon fortification is more than a health fix.

It is an economic decision that can safeguard the next generation, cut avoidable healthcare spending, and strengthen long-term productivity.

World.title: Zulum Donates Multi-Million-Naira JAMB Zonal HQ, 500-Seat CBT Centre to Boost North-east Education
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja





Borno State governor, Prof. Babagana Zulum on Wednesday deepened his administration’s investment in education by handing over a multi-million-naira Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) zonal headquarters and one of Nigeria’s largest Computer-Based Test (CBT) centres, a landmark project expected to transform tertiary admission services across the North-east.

The ultra-modern facility, strategically located along the Maiduguri-Dikwa Road, will serve as JAMB’s North-east Zonal Office, providing administrative and examination services to the region’s six states.

It comprises a modern office complex and a dual CBT centre capable of accommodating 500 candidates simultaneously and processing more than 2,000 candidates daily.

The project is believed to be the first in the country to be wholly financed, constructed and donated by a state government to JAMB.

Commissioning the facility, Zulum described it as part of his administration’s broader strategy to rebuild education in a region that has suffered years of insurgency and disruption to learning.

He said the project was designed not only to improve access to JAMB services but also to strengthen educational infrastructure and reduce the burden on candidates seeking admission into tertiary institutions.

According to the governor, the facility represents Borno State’s contribution to enhancing national education service delivery while positioning the North-east as a major hub for computer-based examinations.

The significance of the project was underscored by JAMB Registrar, Prof. Ishaq Oloyede, who described it as an unprecedented intervention and one of the finest CBT facilities in Nigeria.

“This is the first time in the history of JAMB that a state governor has independently built and donated a zonal office and CBT centre to the Board,” Oloyede said.

He noted that what was initially conceived as an ambitious proposal had become a reality within just four months, describing the achievement as a reflection of Governor Zulum’s visionary leadership and commitment to education.

“Today, reality has surpassed my expectations. In just four months, what seemed humanly impossible has been accomplished,” he said.

Oloyede explained that the centre would significantly expand JAMB’s operational capacity in the North-east by allowing 500 candidates to write examinations simultaneously while handling over 2,000 candidates each day.

He added that the integrated registration facilities would enable the Board to complete registration and documentation for applicants from Borno State within a few days, drastically reducing delays and travel burdens.

“The CBT centre you have graciously provided will serve as a beacon of excellence for computer-based testing and administrative services. It will bring immense relief to candidates, educational institutions and stakeholders across this region.

“More importantly, it represents Your Excellency’s broader commitment to rebuilding educational confidence and expanding opportunities for young people despite the enormous challenges confronting this region,” he stated.

The outgoing JAMB Registrar further commended Governor Zulum’s sustained investment in education, human capital development and youth empowerment, describing education as the foundation for peace, stability and economic recovery in the North-east.

In a symbolic gesture acknowledging Oloyede’s contributions to educational development in Nigeria, Governor Zulum directed the Borno State Ministry of Education to name the newly commissioned facility after the outgoing JAMB Registrar.

The event was attended by the Secretary to the Borno State Government, Bukar Tijani; the incoming JAMB Registrar, Prof. Segun Aina; Acting Chief of Staff to the Governor, Dr. Babagana Mustapha Malumbe; Commissioner for Education, Engr. Lawan Abba Wakilbe; and other senior government officials.

The commissioning marks another milestone in Borno State’s post-insurgency recovery efforts, with the Zulum administration continuing to prioritise investments in schools, tertiary institutions and educational infrastructure as a pathway to rebuilding the state and expanding opportunities for its youth.

World.title: Senate Tightens Noose on Foreign Aid, Moves to Bring NGOs Under Stricter Oversight
World.content:
•Cites accountability gaps, transparency concerns, national security risks

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Senate on Wednesday moved to tighten government oversight of billions of naira in foreign aid and donor-funded interventions by advancing a bill that seeks to subject non-governmental organisations (NGOs), donor agencies and sub-national governments to a more robust regulatory framework.

The proposed legislation, sponsored by Senator Ibrahim Hassan Dankwambo (Gombe North), scaled second reading after lawmakers raised concerns over accountability gaps, financial transparency and potential national security risks arising from the current system of managing foreign grants and humanitarian assistance.

If enacted, the bill will establish a comprehensive legal framework for coordinating, monitoring and integrating all foreign assistance into Nigeria’s fiscal and development planning system.

Leading the debate, Dankwambo said Nigeria remained one of Africa’s largest recipients of grants, concessional financing, humanitarian support and technical assistance from bilateral and multilateral development partners, yet lacked a central mechanism for tracking and coordinating such inflows.

He noted that donor-funded projects were currently scattered across ministries, departments and agencies, with many interventions implemented outside the national budget process, creating room for duplication, weak coordination and poor accountability.

According to him, the proposed legislation is designed to ensure that all foreign assistance received in the country comes under constitutional oversight and aligns with national development priorities.

The bill proposes the establishment of a National Donor Coordination Framework, compulsory registration of all donor-funded projects, and creation of a national database for foreign assistance.

It also seeks the integration of donor interventions into government budgets, mandatory public disclosure of funding and implementation details, as well as sanctions for the diversion, misuse or non-registration of donor funds.

The proposal received overwhelming backing from senators, who argued that huge sums channeled through NGOs and state governments had remained outside effective public scrutiny for years.

Senate Chief Whip, Senator Tahir Monguno, described the bill as timely and necessary, saying donor agencies currently determine the deployment of foreign assistance with little domestic coordination.

Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, observed that while foreign assistance received directly by the Federal Government was usually reflected in the national budget, substantial funds channeled to NGOs and sub-national governments remained largely beyond public oversight.

“We can’t tell what money goes into the coffers of NGOs. Fraudsters set up bogus, pseudo-NGOs and collect money from there,” Barau said.

He maintained that concerns over the lack of transparency in donor funding had lingered for years and urged lawmakers to ensure the legislation was passed.

Senator Adamu Aliero argued that stricter regulation would not only improve the utilisation of donor funds but also strengthen the confidence of development partners by promoting transparency and accountability.

Drawing from previous oversight activities of the Senate Committee on Agriculture, Aliero recalled instances where donor funds were received but their utilisation could not be satisfactorily explained.

He urged that the legislation should expressly cover state governments and NGOs to strengthen the National Assembly’s oversight powers.

Chairman of the Senate Committee on Finance, Senator Sani Musa, said the proposed law would align Nigeria with global best practices while enhancing donor confidence through greater transparency.

He also warned that inadequate scrutiny of donor-funded activities could create security challenges.

“Most of the aids coming to so-called NGOs are not subjected to scrutiny. We have seen instances where such arrangements create security concerns because we do not know who is accounting for what. Is it insurgents taking money meant for victims?” Musa queried.

He added that the legislation would also distinguish foreign investments from grants, thereby improving fiscal planning and policy coordination.

Former Edo State Governor, Senator Adams Oshiomhole, insisted that every donor fund entering Nigeria must be fully disclosed, documented and subjected to legislative oversight.

He called for mandatory disclosure of resources transferred to NGOs and civil society organisations, backed by stringent sanctions for non-compliance.

President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, endorsed the proposal, warning that unregulated foreign funding could constitute a threat to national security if left outside an effective regulatory regime.

Following the debate, the Senate referred the bill to its Committees on National Planning and Economic Development and Finance for further legislative work, directing the panels to submit their report within four weeks.

World.title: IGP Warns Against Illegal Bearing of Arms, Declares Police Will Deal with Any Such Act
World.content:
George Okoh in Makurdi

The Inspector General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has warned against people bearing arms illegally, stating that only the police were recognised to carry arms.

The IG, who spoke at the security stakeholders’ meeting held at the old banquet hall of the Government House, Makurdi, yesterday, said the police were prepared to deal with people possessing illegal arms.

He described the insecurity in Benue State as unacceptable and a source of “sleepless nights” for residents and security agencies.

He stated that Benue was once known as a peaceful and hospitable state but regretted that the state had been overtaken by violence.

He added that the crisis had gone beyond farmer-herder clashes, with criminal gangs, kidnappers and political interests worsening the situation

Condemning the cycle of attacks in the state and reprisals, the IG directed that such must end just as he conveyed President Bola Tinubu’s directive that insecurity in the would no longer be tolerated.

“We are tired of this issue of attack and retaliation. When you attack then you hear of retaliation,

“We are the only ones recognized to carry arms around. No other person is entitled to do that. You cannot move around freely carry arms and think there’s no Law and Order in this country. This will not be tolerated,” he said.

The IG, who warned against unauthorised people bearing arms vowed to crack down on illegal firearms, adding that police officers had been directed to act decisively under Force Order 237 when confronted by armed criminals.

In his speech, Governor Hyacinth Alia of the state, appreciated the visit of the IG, describing it as timely and a demonstration of the Nigeria Police Force’s commitment in tackling insecurity through community policing and collaboration with state governments.

Alia regretted that attacks on communities in the state had resulted in loss of many lives, disruption of farming activities and threatening national food security.

He said his administration had strengthened inter-agency collaboration through regular Security Council meetings, intelligence sharing and coordinated operations, and would continue supporting security personnel and the families of fallen heroes.

World.title: Anambra APC Stakeholders Close Ranks Ahead of 2027 Elections
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

Following the fallout of party primaries that has left the party fractured, the All Progressives Congress (APC) stakeholders in Anambra State have decided to close ranks, reconcile aggrieved members and form a united front ahead of the 2027 general election.

Speaking in Abuja at a stakeholders’ engagement on the leadership crisis in the state, National Deputy Chairman, South, Dr. Benjamin Nwoye, acknowledged the previous attempt to restore peace in the Anambra State chapter of the party.

Nwoye, who is also the Chairman of the FactFinding and Reconciliation Committee, said the mandate of the committee was clear which is to identify the immediate and remote causes of the leadership crisis in the state.

This, he said, further included to engage all relevant stakeholders, reconcile aggrieved members, and recommend measures that would deliver a peaceful, credible and lasting resolution.

He noted that information available to the National Working Committee (NWC) and from preliminary engagements, the issues giving rise to the leadership crisis include the alleged removal of elected party officials at different levels.

Also, part of the issues included alleged removal of names of those who won primary elections and replacement of same with those who never participated in or won the election.

The NWC member said other consideration also included taking the party to court without due process and without exhausting the internal party dispute and grievance resolution mechanisms.

World.title: Bago: Why We’re Demanding 13% Derivation from FG
World.content:
Laleye Dipo in Minna

Niger State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, has defended the decision of the state government to demand 13% derivation from the federal government hinging the request on the effect of the hydro electric dams on communities in the state.

The state currently houses four major hydro electric dams in the country – Jebba, Kainji, Shiroro and Zungeru.

Exchanging views with the the Managing Director of the North Central Development Commission, Mr Cyril Tsenyil, Bago said the disaster caused by the overflows of water from these dams “is enormous” and required substantial funds to remediate the effects before charging the commission to support the governments request for the 13% derivation.

The governor said despite the benefits of the dams to the nations’ economy they have contributed immensely to environmental degradation and loss of lives and property.

Bago also advocated a meeting with his counterparts in the north central geopolitical zone of the country to find solutions to the menace of communal clashes among members of communities in the zone.

The meeting, he said, should be held under the auspices of the newly created Commission but did not recommend the venue noting that communal clashes have become rampant in the zone leading to loss of lives and property therefore requiring joint approach to bring it to a halt.

Such a meeting, Bago said would be an avenue for the commission to fully address other developmental challenges facing the Zone.

The governor commended the commission for doing “remarkably well” but urged it to prioritise the issue of insecurity and communal clashes especially farmer- herder clashes before promising to provide an office for the organisation in Minna.

The Managing Director, of the Commission, Tsenyil, said the Commission was committed to building a strong partnership based on the Act establishing it which included planning and implementing of programmes for sustainable development across the north central region.

Tsenyil added that such activities covered the areas of transportation, roads, healthcare,education, agriculture, industrialization, water supply, electricity and telecommunications.

World.title: Malnutrition Costs Nigeria More than Oil Pipeline Vandalism, Power Outages Combined
World.content:
Okon Bassey in Uyo

The Chairman, House of Representatives Committee on Nutrition and Food Security, Dr. Chike John Okafor, has said that malnutrition costs Nigeria more than oil pipeline vandalism and power outages combined.

The federal lawmaker who presented a keynote address at a 3-day National Strategic Policy Dialogue going on in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State capital stressed that nutrition is not a social welfare issue, but an economic issue.

He said according to the World Bank, “Nigeria loses $2.5 billion annually to malnutrition. That is 12% of our GDP gone to reduced productivity, healthcare costs, and lost potential”.

The 2026 Legislative Strategic Policy Dialogue with the Theme: “Strengthening Legislative Action for Improved Nutrition Outcomes in Nigeria”, has participants drawn from national stakeholders and legislators.

He reasoned that nutrition is one of the best investments any government can make as every $1 invested in nutrition generates $16 in economic returns.

“Good nutrition leads to healthier children, better learning outcomes, a more productive workforce, and ultimately, faster GDP growth.”

Hon Okafor regretted that 32% of our children under 5 are stunted, 7.1% wasted, while 58% of women of reproductive age are anaemic.

He posited that with the inauguration of the House Committee on Nutrition and Food Security in Feb 2024, and the launch of the National Legislative Network, we now have the institutional platform to act.

“The National Legislative Network on Nutrition and Food Security, comprising of my committee, and those of the 36 State Houses of Assembly, was therefore inaugurated in the House of Representatives on July 20, 2024 to pursue a holistic, nationwide approach to mitigate malnutrition and food insecurity.

“With the inauguration of the House Committee on Nutrition and Food Security in Feb 2024, and the launch of the National Legislative Network, we now have the institutional platform to act.”

Expressing worry over the funding gap, he said currently, less than 0.5% of the federal budget goes to nutrition-specific interventions even when experts estimate that we need at least 1.5% to meet global targets.

“I therefore call on this State Houses of Assembly to ring-fence nutrition budget lines in the appropriation; ensure timely release of approved funds; mandate quarterly reporting from MDAs.”

As a call to action, “let us move from appropriation to outcomes; to my fellow legislators: approve the budgets; conduct oversight in your constituencies and champion nutrition laws. To MDAs: Deliver results and share data transparently. To the Private Sector and CSOs: Partner with government to scale solutions.”

He emphasized that a well-nourished child becomes a productive student, a skilled worker, and a contributing citizen; adding that a well-nourished Nigeria is a wealthy Nigeria.

“Let us, as legislators and stakeholders, commit today to turning Nigeria’s demographic potential into a demographic dividend.”, he stated.

This high-level dialogue will convene Speakers and Committee Chairpersons of State Houses of Assembly from 17 focal states: Akwa Ibom, Enugu, Bayelsa, Jigawa, Sokoto, Gombe, Adamawa, Kebbi, Zamfara, Cross River, FCT, Kano, Nasarawa, Kaduna, Niger, Bauchi, and Lagos, alongside Permanent Secretaries, State Nutrition Officers, Development Partners and CSOs to secure legislative commitment.

The dialogue is to canvas for increase domestic funding for nutrition and institutionalize the Child Nutrition Fund (CNF); advance 6 months paid maternity leave policies; strengthen accountability and integrate nutrition into constituency project; establish Legislative Nutrition Champions to anchor nutrition in state agendas.

World.title: How much is Saturday Lotto and Lotto Plus worth?
World.content:
How much is Saturday Lotto and Lotto Plus worth on 25 July 2026? Well, it breaks down like so: After a big payout this week, straight Lotto is worth R2 million, Lotto Plus 1 sits at R3.5 million and for Lotto Plus Max 5 tag on another R1 million. All tallied up that put’s the total worth of the Saturday game at R6.5 million.



Crucial to your success in Saturday Lotto and Lotto Plus is knowing how recently one of the three lottos has paid out. A bit like the old days playing slot machines in the casino, the longer it goes, the bigger the payout becomes. Looking at the above figures, we can see that almost all have paid relatively recently. This has been one of the criticisms of the new game mechanics – that payouts, while more frequent, rarely climb to remarkable numbers anymore.

SATURDAY LOTTO AND LOTTO PLUS

As such, Saturday Lotto and Lotto Plus has always been the National Lottery’s kind of bread-and-butter game. Cheaper than PowerBall and PowerBall XTRA, easier to win, but less dramatic when it comes to jackpots. Nevertheless, Sizekhaya’s 1 June 2026 takeover reshaped it even further. The core mechanics require players to choose six numbers from a pool of 1 to 52, which is reduced from 1 to 58 previously.

As ever, numbers can be chosen manually or auto generated through the popular Quick Pick. Pricing sits lower than PowerBall’s controversial increase. A standard Lotto board costs R5, with Lotto Plus 1 adding R2.50 and Lotto 5 Max adding a further R2.50 on top. Therefore, playing all three together costs R10 per board.

What players are still wrapping their head around is the new MultiPlay (MP1) option. It lets players add a seventh number to their existing six in each of the three games. And it gets proportionally more expensive as you go. The total combination if you add MP1 across all boards is R70 – that’s R35 + R17.50 + R17.50. However, your odds are massively improved if you do go down this rabbit hole.

HOW TO HANDLE MULTIPLAY

A big winner this past week reduces the Saturday Lotto and Lotto Plus takings. Image: File

Therefore, add MP1 to Saturday Lotto and Lotto Plus across all three games and your total ticket will cost R70.00. However, if you’re using your banking app, be sure to lookout for digital banking fee of roughly R2.95 added to the transaction. So, the question remains, is it worth spending so much extra money? Well, let’s look at the sums …

Jackpot odds have already improved substantially under the new number matrix. The chances of matching all six numbers now sits at 1 in 20 million. That’s twice as likely as the old 1 in 40 million under ITHUBA. However, dabble with the MP1 and all of a sudden, you’re playing with seven numbers instead of six. This means your odds now become just 1 in 2.9 million, which represents a straight sevenfold improvement. And don’t forget that’s across all three games since they share the board.



DRAW TIMES AND CLAIMING LOTTO AND LOTTO PLUS WINNINGS

Lotto and Lotto Plus draw every Wednesday and Saturday at 21:00. Sizekhaya brought back live televised draws using physical machines. Ticket sales cut off half an hour before the draw typically at 20:30. Entries can be done in-person in store or through digital banking apps. All lottery prizes must be claimed within 365 days of the draw date. Anyone who misses that window forfeits their prize and the money is transferred to the National Lottery Distribution Trust for to assist the needy through charitable causes.

Remember, if you’re a SASSA beneficiary and money is tight playing Saturday Lotto and Lotto Plus, decide on a budget before buying lotto tickets, and don’t chase a bad week by spending more. The National Responsible Gambling Programme runs a toll-free counselling line on 0800 006 008 for anyone who is struggling. As ever, how and where to claim Saturday Lotto and Lotto Plus winnings depends on the amount won:

Small prizes (up to R4 999 ) get paid out directly at licensed retailers.

) can be claimed at selected partner banks. Anything above R50 000 requires an in-person visit to a Sizekhaya regional office, with the original ticket and a valid South African ID.

Anyone unsure where to start can call the Sizekhaya helpline on 0861 026 000. Or you can visit one of the eight regional offices nationally:

Therefore, checking old ticket numbers against those drawn (up to one year ago) costs you nothing and might just turn up forgotten money. You can do so by clicking past results HERE.

World.title: Trevor Noah: ‘Why I want my kids to grow up in SA’ [video]
World.content:
Trevor Noah wants his children to grow up in South Africa. Images via Facebook/ Canva

Despite being an internationally acclaimed entertainer, Trevor Noah wants his future children to grow up in South Africa.



The comedian was born in Soweto to a black, Xhosa mother and a white, Swiss father, with his mixed-race background considered a “crime” under Apartheid.

In 2011, he relocated to the US, where he is now a naturalised citizen.

TREVOR NOAH: ‘I WANT MY KIDS TO GROW UP IN SA’

In a clip he shared from a recent stand-up skit, Trevor Noah revealed why he wanted his future kids to have a childhood in South Africa.

He said: “I would want them to grow up in a country where you have multiple cultures…multiple languages, in a country where you understand that there are other ways to be…where there’s diversity of thought, in terms of food. I want them to live here and know here. I want them to be South African”.

He continued: “I want my kids to have grit. I want them to have texture. You take for granted what a child growing up in South Africa learns. You take for granted what they have to go through. It makes you something special. You know, it polishes you, a diamond from the rough.

“The most important reason I want to have children who are South African is because I want children who have culture and respect. You take that for granted as a South African, the way we treat each other. Even in the toughest times, you take it for granted because you’re here. South Africans, we are truly a cut above the rest.



Trevor Noah jokingly compared South African children to American kids, whom he claimed were “demons”.

‘BORN A CRIME’

Trevor Noah was born in 1984 to Patricia and Robert Noah. He grew up with his mother and his maternal grandmother in Soweto.

Trevor was a product of an interracial relationship, which was illegal under the Apartheid-era Immorality Act.

His childhood inspired the title of his memoir, Born a Crime.

World.title: ‘Stop using it at the ATM’: SASSA grant beneficiaries share Black Card warning
World.content:
Postbank is pushing millions of social grant beneficiaries to swap their SASSA Gold Cards for new Black Cards before the 31 August deadline, but many who have already made the switch say the new card is bringing problems of its own.



Frustration has been spilling onto social media, with grant recipients sharing experiences of network failures, missing payments and poor customer support after receiving their new Postbank Black Cards.

Makhosetive Banele was among those who voiced concern, writing: “Those black cards still giving us problem yesterday we couldn’t get it who is fooling who, we are still going to suffer even more.”

Siphokazi Sporo Chawekazi James shared a similar experience: “Am using Postbank but I didn’t get the money.”

Sesi Patricia went further, warning others not to make the switch at all: “Pls don’t change to the Black Card is very useless if u have a problem with the Card no one will help u.”

Some urge beneficiaries to use their own bank accounts instead of Black Cards

A number of commenters are advising beneficiaries to bypass the Black Card altogether and redirect their grants to a personal bank account. One commenter wrote: “Run way dont do black please this card with network problems go SASSA fast and change to use BANK OF YOUR OWN.”

Keke Keketso added a practical tip for those already holding Black Cards: “Guys with black cards stop using those card at ATM you gonna have problems just do cash backs.”



Despite the complaints, Postbank has made its position clear that the Gold Card will stop working after 31 August, and that date will not be extended under any circumstances. Beneficiaries who have not yet made the switch have only one grant payment cycle left to do so.

Postbank Chief Commercial Officer Thami Cele warned that anyone without a Black Card after the deadline will need to obtain one before they can access any payments, meaning a missed grant month is a real risk for those who delay.

What you need to know before you go

The replacement process is free of charge and available at Postbank service points inside Shoprite, Checkers, Usave, Pick n Pay, Boxer and Spar stores. Beneficiaries need only bring a valid ID, no forms, no signatures. Any balance on the Gold Card transfers automatically to the new card, and no SASSA office visit is required.

For those experiencing problems with their Black Cards, Postbank’s toll-free helpline is available on 0800 5354 55. To find the nearest collection point, dial *120*355#

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: We Buy Cars responds to ‘offensive’ refugee ad [video]
World.content:
We Buy Cars have responded to social media backlash to its advert depicting a South African refugee. Image via YouTube screenshot

We Buy Cars has responded to the social media backlash of its recent , which depicted a white, Afrikaner family that relocated to the US under the refugee programme.

The ad has been met with strong opposition from the Afrikaner community, including some who have now resettled in America.

According to US government-released data, close to 8 000 primarily white South Africans have arrived in the country under President Donald Trump’s initiative for racial minorities,



based on his unproven claims of racial persecution and land reform policies.

WE BUY CARS RESPOND TO BACKLASH OVER ‘REFUGEE’ ADVERT

This week, We Buy Cars trended on social media platforms over an advert that was released last month.

In it, the car-buying company depicted two South African families – a black and white, Afrikaner one – who met in the US during the FIFA World Cup. While the black family arrived to watch the sporting tournament, the Afrikaner family joked about receiving a free trip to America under Trump’s refugee programme.

Responding to criticism from the Afrikaner community, We Buy Cars told Newsday: “This YouTube ad was created to celebrate sport as something that brings South Africans together, during Bafana Bafana’s World Cup campaign.

“We understand the campaign has been received differently by some viewers, and we appreciate the feedback being shared.

“Mockery was never the intention. WeBuyCars serves customers across every community in South Africa, and we remain mindful of that in the work we put out.”



SORRY, NOT SORRY?

It’s not the first time We Buy Cars has appeared to have poked fun at Trump’s refugee resettlement programme.

In April last year, just weeks before the first group of South Africans took up “refugee status”, the company aired an advert titled “Rev-Jou-Jeep status”.

The cheeky ad won the Creative Visionary Award at the 2025 YouTube Works Awards South Africa.

World.title: Orlando Pirates news: Matuludi, Radiopane, Appollis, Xoki
World.content:
Orlando Pirates conclude their pre-season in Spain after three weeks of intensive training.

The team played a number of high profile teams, earning two wins and will return home full of confidence having impressed not just only the technical team but fans.

All their games were broadcasted on their YouTube channel, giving the fans a taste of what’s to come for next season.



So far, Orlando Pirates have made seven new signings but have been linked with a few players in recent weeks.

One of the players likely to join the Buccaneers is Thabang Matuludi.

KickOff reported that Polokwane City were currently weighing up offers from both Orlando Pirates and Sundowns.

“The boss wants a little bit of space to choose the right offer for both the player and the club.

“He has agreed to sell the player and he is expected to leave the club,” a source told the publication.

From a football perspective, Orlando Pirates may present the more attractive destination for Matuludi. The Buccaneers are looking to strengthen at right-back and could offer him a clearer path to regular first-team football.



Currently, Deano van Rooyen and Kamohelo Sebelebele are Pirates’ recognised options on the right side of defence, although Sebelebele is also capable of playing further forward. That could open the door for Matuludi to compete immediately for a starting role.

Which Orlando Pirates players could leave?

The club parted ways with the likes of Sipho Mbule and Thabiso Lebitso last month but it wouln’t be a surprise if the Buccaneers announce more departures.

Boitumelo Radiopane, who has not featured much under Abdeslam Ouaddou last season, was linked to a potential permanent exit as the club looks for a top striker.

His impressive two goals in Spain has now almost cemented his stay for next season and might warrant a start next weekend when the Betway Premiership kicks off.

Oswin Appollis was tipped to leave Orlando Pirates after the FIFA World Cup but it appears he might stay for another season. He was given a few days off after the tournament but later joined the squad in Spain thus confirming that he will stay in Mayfair.

Ex-Bucs captain Tapelo Xoki wasn’t played much in two years however, he has extended his stay.

World.title: Pensioners complain about missing SASSA grant payments
World.content:
Buried beneath the usual debate over payment dates and grant amounts, a quieter but more urgent complaint has been surfacing on The South African’s Facebook page: beneficiaries saying their SASSA Older Persons Grant didn’t come through at all.



Cecil Walter Price’s comment was short, but it struck a nerve. “I didn’t get my old age this month,” he wrote.

For pensioners who rely on the grant as their only source of income, a missed payment isn’t a minor inconvenience. It’s rent, electricity, and groceries that go unpaid, with no clear timeline for when or whether the money will land.

A system pensioners say has stopped working for them

The missed-payment complaints landed alongside a separate, longer-running grievance about who the grant is actually for. Judi Black raised the point directly, arguing that decades of contribution should count for something: “We have paid taxes for more than 65 years, all our working lives, yet we don’t qualify for” a sentence that trailed into more complaints about the means test cutting people out.

Read together, the two threads paint a picture of pensioners who feel doubly let down, first by a grant they say excludes people who contributed to the tax system for most of their lives, and second by a payment system that, according to some commenters, doesn’t reliably deliver even to those who do qualify.

What the agency says vs what beneficiaries are experiencing

SASSA’s official position is that the Older Persons Grant pays out on the second working day of each month, currently R2 400 for those aged 60 and older. Beneficiaries who don’t receive a payment are advised to wait two to three business days before contacting SASSA directly, since banks can occasionally process deposits later than the agency’s own release date.

But for commenters like Cecil Walter Price, that advice offers little comfort when the grant is the only income keeping a household afloat. Whether these are isolated banking delays or a wider pattern remains unclear, but the volume of replies suggests he isn’t the only one watching his account and waiting.

World.title: St David’s Marist honours Luqobo Makwedini with his iconic ‘Felicia’ war cry [video]
World.content:
The learners at St David’s Marist, Inanda performed the iconic war cry in honour of the late Luqobo “Bibo” Makwedini at their school. Their heartfelt act proves just how inspirational and unforgettable he truly was.



ST DAVID’S MARIST HONOURS LUQOBO ‘BIBO’ MAKWEDINI

The learners performed the “Felicia” war cry, which catapulted Luqobo into internet stardom while he was still schooling at Wynberg Boys’ High School, Cape Town, in 2023.

In a tribute shared by St David’s on social media, Luqobo’s legacy reflects his profound impact on his peers and people across the world, showing how sports can bring people together.

“Some moments are bigger than sport. Our boys came together to honour Luqobo Makwedini by performing his iconic war cry rendition “Felicia uyashisa [she’s hot]”, a tribute to the passion, pride and spirit that continue to inspire South Africans.”

“May this be a reminder that sport has the power to unite, uplift and leave a legacy that echoes far beyond the final whistle. Thank you, Luqobo, for giving our boys a moment they’ll never forget.”

Mahlokileng commented: Love the energy, boys. Thanks for paying homage to the legend he was.



Olivestsholo wrote: Oh, what a sweet moment. Forever in our hearts. Well done, Inanda.

Fiksm2000 added: Thank you, boys; he’ll be missed.

LUQOBO MAKWEDINI’S PASSING SHOOK MANY

Many people were shocked by the news of Luqobo Makwedini’s passing on 11 July, as he was young and had a promising future within the rugby fraternity.

The 20-year-old collapsed during a training session in France. Although the cause of his death remains unknown, reports indicate he suffered cardiac arrest.

Luqobo moved to France in 2025 after joining his new rugby home AS Béziers Hérault for the upcoming 2025/2026 season.



His former school, Wynberg Boys’ High School, shared the following tribute on social media:

“Our Wynberg community mourns the tragic passing of our much-loved brother, Bibo Makwedini, Matric 2025. Our thoughts and prayers are with his family, teammates, and school friends. RIP Old Boy, Old Friend.”

World.title: Who’s the Boss? Designer-clad Peet Viljoen vows to practise law again
World.content:
Peet Viljoen returned to court to continue his bail application. Images via X

Disbarred attorney Peet Viljoen has vowed to practise law again despite mounting criminal allegations against him. The husband of reality TV star Mel Viljoen returned to the Specialised Commercial Crime Court in Pretoria, where he continued his bail application.

Peet ditched his Hugo Boss tracksuit, which he has worn for the past three consecutive appearances, for a branded Boss T-shirt under a grey suit. The 57-year-old – who is being remanded in custody at the Kgosi Mampuru Correctional Centre – is facing 400 charges of fraud, theft, corruption and forgery.

The court has reserved judgment until 17 August.



PEET VILJOEN WANTS TO PRACTISE LAW AGAIN

On Thursday, 23 July, Peet Viljoen returned to the Specialised Commercial Crime Court in Pretoria, where he continued his application to be released on bail pending trial.

In an affidavit handed to the court, Peet offered to pay R250,000 in bail, submit to house arrest, surrender his passport, and report daily to police.

He also claimed that he would not abscond and would willingly face the 400 charges of fraud, theft, corruption and forgery laid against him by the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA).

Wearing an apt “Boss” designer T-shirt, Peet also revealed that he was hopeful he would practise law again and was in the process of submitting an application to be placed on the court roll for his return.

In his affidavit, Peet Viljoen also defended his social media posts as a “constitutional right to freedom of expression”, maintained that he was not a flight risk and claimed that it was in the “interest of justice” that he was released on bail.

He also argued that the state’s case is “weak” and “flawed” and shared how he intends to sue the NPA for R500 million for unlawful prosecution.



Breaking news



The Pretoria Specialised Commercial Crimes Court has reserved judgment until 17 August 2026 in disbarred attorney Peet Viljoen's contested bail application.



Viljoen is facing more than 400 charges, including fraud, corruption, theft, forgery and uttering, linked… pic.twitter.com/eBDbOIys5i — MDN NEWS (@MDNnewss) July 23, 2026

WHAT CHARGES IS HE FACING?

Peet Viljoen is facing 400 charges, including fraud, corruption, theft, forgery, uttering and related offences relating to the illegal sale of Johannesburg municipal properties estimated at R27 million.

Along with five others, the NPA has alleged that Peet forged sale agreements, municipal resolutions, and affidavits, and unlawfully used his powers of attorney to transfer municipal properties.

They also allege that he bribed a deputy registrar to facilitate the transactions.

World.title: Witness claims Mapisa-Nqakula asked for bribe
World.content:
PRETORIA - The High Court in Pretoria has heard how former Defence Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula allegedly made her first personal request for a bribe from a Defence Department contractor.



Nombasa Ntsondwa-Ndlhovu, who has admitted to paying Mapisa-Nqakula R4.5 million in bribes, testified that the former minister’s first direct request was for R200,000.



This was during a meeting at a hotel near OR Tambo International Airport.



The defence insisted that the State clarify whether the indemnity it intends to grant Nombasa Ntshondwa-Ndlovu for testifying against Mapisa-Nqakula will also apply to the separate criminal charges she faces in another court.



Judge Mashudu Munzhelele ruled that she has no jurisdiction to grant indemnity in relation to charges pending

before another court.



Meanwhile, the court has barred the media from broadcasting any audio or video footage of the witness.



Ntsondwa-Ndlhovu is expected to continue her testimony on Friday.



eNCA's Moloko Moloto reports in the video above.

World.title: BOSA fires Ayanda Allie
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Build One South Africa (BOSA) has terminated Ayanda Allie’s membership in the party.

The party confirmed the news in a statement on Thursday, saying the decision follows the conclusion of an internal disciplinary process.

READ | BOSA takes legal action against government over water crisis

The process dates back to July 2025

“Over an extended period, BOSA undertook repeated efforts through engagement, consultation and mediation to resolve the matter amicably. "Despite these efforts, it became evident that there was no viable basis upon which the matter could be resolved,” the statement reads in part.

According to the party, Allie was afforded the opportunity to appeal the Board's decision but has elected not to exercise that right.

“The Board's decision is therefore final,” the statement further said.

Allie served as a member of the Gauteng Provincial Legislature

World.title: Winter Initiation Season | The dangerous journey of becoming a man
World.content:
KUGOMPO CITY - The Eastern Cape has recorded 14 deaths during the Winter Initiation Season, four fewer than Mpumalanga.

Among the biggest culprits are illegally established schools that don't comply with health and safety regulations.

To make matters worse for authorities, many of these schools are hidden away in remote areas, which are hard to find.

The tradition has been described as something that's become a death trap for many young initiates.

Some have even said the practice of traditional circumcision will continue to see more lives being lost unless the old ways of doing things start to change.

While the Department of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs (Cogta) continues to grapple with the unscrupulous behaviour of some individuals, others argue they are relying too much on modern medicine to heal young initiates and are sidelining traditional medicine and culture.

Cogta said that at least 40 people were arrested, 58 illegal initiation schools shut down, and 116 criminal cases opened.

While those numbers reflect that authorities are trying to clamp down on those choosing to put children's lives at risk at the expense of making money, the reality remains that one life lost is still far too many.

eNCA's Ronald Masinda reports in the video above.

World.title: Clock is ticking, change SASSA gold card or risk payment disruption
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Less than 39 days remain for SASSA gold card beneficiaries to switch to the new Postbank Black Card before the 31 August deadline.

Beneficiaries who fail to migrate risk disruptions to their social grant payments.

This as the gold cards will be phased out and will no longer be accepted after the deadline.

According to Postbank spokesperson Bongani Diako, necessary resources to support beneficiaries during the card migration programme have been put in place.

READ | SASSA beneficiaries urged to switch to Black Cards before deadline

However, he said the success of the programme also depends on beneficiaries taking advantage of the time that remains and ensuring that they replace their cards from our sites as soon as possible.

"Beneficiaries are strongly encouraged not to wait until the August payment dates, or final days of the migration period, to switch their cards to avoid last-minute queue congestion at our service points and ensure a seamless transition," Diako added.

World.title: Carrim's Madlanga Commission testimony to be held in open
World.content:
PRETORIA - North West businessman Suliman Carrim will testify in an open session before the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry on Friday.

The Commission confirmed this ruling on Thursday, rejecting Carrim's application for in-camera proceedings for the second time.

The first application was denied in March. This saw him testify in an open session.

The Commission's reasoning at the time was that Carrim's legal team had not filed its application on time.

READ | WATCH | Suleiman Carrim denied in-camera testimony

Part of the conditions of the recent ruling includes that the commission and legal representatives of Carrim are prohibited from mentioning his medical condition.

This includes the nature of the treatment he is receiving, the identity and nature of the practice of the health professionals attending to Carrim in respect of the medical condition, and the medical facility where he is admitted.

Another condition is that the names of residential and business addresses belonging to Carrim's family may not be mentioned.

READ | Carrim's testimony at Madlanga Commission delayed amid hospitalisation

Carrim’s appearance before the Madlanga Commission is long overdue.

He missed his scheduled appearance before the Commission last month to continue his testimony following an earlier postponement linked to health concerns.

The Commission was informed that Carrim was medically unfit to testify, resulting in his appearance being rescheduled.

World.title: Jordaan explodes over Broos reports: 'It's nonsense!'
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - “South Africans must just wait”, the fighting words of SAFA President Danny Jordaan when quizzed about the saga involving the national head coach.

This comes after weeks of confusion and mixed messaging on coach Hugo Broos' Bafana Bafana future.

“One thing I can say is that there is no such thing as SAFA signed a one-year contract with Broos,” Jordaan said.

“It doesn't exist. It's nonsense and it's better that this nonsense is not put out there.

There have been media reports that Broos has reportedly been given a one-year contract extension to stay on as Bafana Bafana coach for next year's Afcon.

There seems to be confusion regarding the Belgian-born coach's future in South Africa.

Broos had indicated that he planned to retire after guiding Bafana Bafana at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

However, there is now uncertainty about whether he plans to continue leading Bafana or not.

eNCA's Thabiso Sithole's quest for clarity from SAFA was greeted by a fiery Jordaan.

“So I just came back yesterday and I saw what is this now? It's nonsense,” Jordaan said.

“There is a process. You cannot stop me in the street and hijack a decision. It's not going to happen.

Broos helped guide South Africa to back-to-back AFCON qualifications, a bronze medal at the 2023 tournament in the Ivory Coast, and the country's first-ever FIFA World Cup knock-out appearance at this past World Cup.

World.title: Ramaphosa unveils national rescue plan to deal with water crisis
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - President Cyril Ramaphosa has released a National Water Action Plan aimed at securing a reliable water supply for the country.

The plan lays out practical steps to tackle the root causes of the country's water crisis, including ageing infrastructure, struggling municipalities and corruption in the sector.

It was developed by the National Water Crisis Committee, which was set up after this year's State of the Nation Address.

READ | Majodina vows crackdown on water tanker mafia

Ramaphosa said the government wants to replicate the approach used to tackle load shedding, with the goal of restoring reliable water services.

The plan brings together all spheres of government and other key partners to drive implementation.
