World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Four curated spaces. Two unforgettable nights. Over 50 world-class artists.

For anyone walking into the Sandton International Convention Centre this September, the biggest hurdle will not be finding great music – it will be managing the sheer volume of choices.

World.title: Murkomen: Police no longer rely on Gachagua's 'gossip'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen during the official launch of the Multi-biometric Identification System (MBIS) and handover ceremony of ANSI National Accreditation Board Certificate at DCI Headquarters on July 23, 2026. [NPS]

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has accused former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua of spreading falsehoods, saying technology-driven policing has replaced "gossip-based" investigations.

Speaking during the handover of the ANSI National Accreditation Board certification to the Forensic Evidence Management Unit and the launch of the Multi-Biometric Identification System at the Directorate of Criminal Investigations headquarters on Thursday, Murkomen said the country has shifted from outdated investigative methods to science-based policing.

"We are moving away from gossip-based collection of evidence to science. I saw an impeached former leader claiming he is well connected to police officers and receives gossip every day because he is not busy unlike the President," said Murkomen.

He said the biometric system will strengthen investigations through science and technology, making unofficial information unnecessary.

"That is an old style of collecting evidence. We now have a modern police service driven by science and technology. We do not need his gossip to run the National Police Service," he observed.

Murkomen claimed the technology would make it harder for unsuitable individuals to rise through public office.

"If these systems had been in place many years ago, people like Gachagua would not have survived the system as habitual offenders until he slipped through to become Deputy President. Such things will never happen again with this technological advancement," said Murkomen.

The Interior CS defended Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja, saying he has the government's confidence and has discharged his duties professionally.

"I have full support and faith in the leadership of the Inspector General. He has carried out his duties with dignity, honour and respect for the citizens of Kenya and his office," noted Murkomen.

Murkomen also rejected Gachagua's criticism of police leadership, arguing that Kenya is recording fewer cases of terrorism, banditry, robbery and other crimes.

"There has never been a period when Kenya has recorded fewer incidents of terrorism, banditry, robberies and other crimes. Our security agencies are working together and have improved security," he said.

He also criticised remarks attributed to Gachagua warning tourists against visiting Kenya, saying they damage the country's reputation.

"For anyone to stand out there and say Kenya is not safe and tourists should not come to our country is very embarrassing," explained Murkomen.

Murkomen dismissed claims that 68 women were raped by police officers during the Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election, urging anyone with evidence to report the matter to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority or the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights.

"If those incidents occurred, they should be reported so those responsible can be held accountable. If not, those making such reckless statements must also be held accountable," said Murkomen.

He accused Gachagua of making the allegations out of political desperation.

"I know why Gachagua speaks the way he does. It is because of desperation. Knowing that he cannot hold any office again in Kenya and can never be President of this republic, he wants to take the entire nation, including the economy, down the drain with himself. We will not allow that," he said.

Murkomen also urged media organisations to challenge politicians they host instead of allowing false claims to go unchecked.

"We should not feed Kenyans with lies. I want to tell media houses that when you invite such reckless human beings, please carry with you a lie detector. Otherwise you are going to mislead the people of Kenya and drive bad behaviour in our country," said Murkomen.

He maintained that intelligence gathering within the National Police Service follows lawful procedures and dismissed claims that private individuals receive confidential police briefings outside official channels

World.title: Gachagua: Why Ruto will not steal the 2027 General Election
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Righathi Gachagua during a live interview with KTN at his Karen home, Nairobi. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has claimed that President William Ruto will not be able to manipulate the outcome of the 2027 General Election, arguing that Kenyans have become more vigilant in protecting their votes.

Speaking during a live interview with KTN from his Karen residence, the former Deputy President said the recent Ol Kalou by-election had provided opposition supporters with a blueprint on safeguarding the electoral process.

"Voting is not enough; you vote and protect the vote. We now have a template from the Ol Kalou by-election," Gachagua said.

He urged Kenyans to remain vigilant during the next General Election, saying the alleged intimidation witnessed in Ol Kalou had failed to influence voters.

"They tried intimidating the people of Ol Kalou, but they did not succeed. We are celebrating what happened, and people from across the country are calling to benchmark on how it worked," he said.

Gachagua also questioned the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC)'s ability to conduct a free and fair election, accusing the electoral body of failing to condemn alleged voter suppression and bribery during the Ol Kalou by-election.

"IEBC has not even condemned the wrongs that happened during the by-election in Ol Kalou. We lost two people who were actually protecting our votes," he alleged.

The DCP leader further renewed his criticism of President Ruto, accusing him of betraying voters from the Mt Kenya region despite earlier warnings.

According to Gachagua, the outcome of the Ol Kalou by-election should serve as a warning to the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He maintained that the by-election demonstrated that Kenyans could no longer be intimidated by the State and described the result as a preview of what to expect in the next national polls.

Gachagua also revisited the Mbeere North by-election, alleging that DCP lost because of widespread voter bribery, intimidation of elderly voters and failure by the party to adequately protect its votes.

"We lost the Mbeere North by-election because we didn't protect our votes properly. There was also massive voter bribery, and those who participated were allegedly given the balance of their bribe after showing a photo of whom they had voted for," he claimed.

The former Deputy President further argued that DCP would have secured an even larger victory in Ol Kalou were it not for what he described as voter suppression and police intimidation.



More to follow...

World.title: Charles Owino appointed as Government Spokesperson
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

President William Ruto has promoted Government Spokesperson Isaac Mwaura in a fresh round of changes within the Executive, while also making nominations to key constitutional commissions and statutory bodies.

In an Executive Order issued on Tuesday, Chief of Staff and Head of Public Service Felix Koskei said the Public Service Commission had approved promotions and redeployments affecting senior government officials.

Under the changes, Mwaura was promoted and redesignated as the Head of the Office of Diversity, Inclusion and Disability Rights in the Executive Office of the President.

Charles Owino Wahong’o was redeployed from the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy to the Executive Office of the President, where he will serve as Acting Head of Government Communications.

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

At the same time, Ruto also nominated new office holders to key constitutional commissions and approved changes within the senior ranks of the Executive in a fresh round of appointments aimed at filling vacancies and strengthening government institutions.

Among the nominees is Dr. Duncan Ojwang Oburu, who has been picked to serve as the Chairperson of the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA).

Ruto also nominated Ms. Antonina Lentoijoni and former Kenya National Union of Teachers (KNUT) Secretary-General Wilson Sossion as members of the Teachers Service Commission (TSC).

Ms. Flora Mutua was nominated as a member of the Public Service Commission (PSC).

In the nominations, Ruto also named seven individuals to serve on the Intergovernmental Relations Technical Committee (IGRTC), subject to ratification by the National and County Government Co-ordinating Summit in accordance with the Intergovernmental Relations Act.

The nominees are Wilson Kuria Thuita (Murang'a), Silvya C. Apaa (Busia), Ahmed Kanyara Bishar (Wajir), Pascalyne Ntang'enoi Kimiriri (Laikipia), Ken Riaga (Migori), Evalyn Chepkirui Aruasa (Nakuru) and Mary Nanjala Kilobi (Nairobi).

World.title: Why public servants have less than a month to update pension records
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Public servants given until August 14 to update pension records [File]

Government has directed all public servants to update their records with the Public Service Superannuation Fund (PSSF) by August 14, 2026, in the latest step towards modernising pension administration.

In a circular signed by Principal Secretary for Public Service and Human Capital Development Dr Jane Imbunya, all PSSF members are expected to update their personal information and beneficiary details through the PSSF Member Self-Service Portal or the PSSF Mobile Application.

The circular was addressed to Ministries, State Departments, Constitutional Commissions, Independent Offices, County Public Service Boards and County Governments.

The exercise is expected to streamline pension administration and accelerate the processing of retirement benefits supported by a new Pension Administration System (PAS), a digital platform developed by PSSF to deliver faster, more transparent and more efficient pension services.

The registration exercise targets 529,635 members drawn from across the public service, including 332,950 teachers under the Teachers Service Commission (TSC), 120,084 officers in the disciplined services, 60,322 employees in Ministries, Departments, Constitutional Commissions and Agencies (MDCAs), and 16,279 county government employees.

PSSF Chief Executive Jonah Aiyabei said updating member records is critical to the success of the pension reforms and the delivery of efficient retirement services.

“By updating their records, public servants will enable quicker processing of retirement benefits, reduce administrative delays, improve data integrity, allow members to access pension services seamlessly through digital channels and ensure that the right benefits reach the right beneficiaries at the right time,” he said.

Under the new system, members can access their pension statements in real time, monitor contributions, view projected retirement benefits, update beneficiary nominations and personal details and initiate and track pension claims remotely.

The platform also features a Sponsor Portal that enables employer institutions to submit payroll information, contribution schedules and member data electronically, significantly improving efficiency and accountability in pension administration.

Dr Aiyabei said the Pension Administration System marks a significant milestone in the government’s efforts to digitise pension administration and restore dignity to retirees through faster, more accessible and transparent services.

“It will provide our members with real-time access to their pension information, enable seamless engagement with the Fund and support a fully digital, paperless pension administration process. Ultimately, our goal is to restore dignity in old age by ensuring every public servant receives timely and efficient pension services,” he said.

World.title: Inside Kenya's Ebola defences as seven Americans enter quarantine
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

A doctor provides care to a patient with Ebola virus disease at the Rwampara Ebola Treatment Centre (ETC) in Bunia, Ituri, July 13, 2026. [AFP]

Seven American humanitarian workers are spending 21 days under medical observation in Kenya not because they are ill, but because they could become ill.

A Reuters report published today confirms they are seven American Disaster Assistance Response Team (DART) staff from the Christian humanitarian organisation Samaritan's Purse . Franklin Graham, the organisation's President and CEO, confirmed this, saying:

“Samaritan's Purse has seven American Disaster Assistance Response Team staff members there. None of them have any symptoms, but they are being quarantined by the Kenyan government for 21 days."

The aid workers, all returning from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where they were involved in responding to the world's largest recorded outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, have no symptoms and have not tested positive for the virus.

Yet under new US public health rules, they cannot travel home immediately. Instead, they are completing a precautionary quarantine on Kenyan soil.

Their arrival has reignited debate over Kenya's role in regional outbreak preparedness and raised a question that extends far beyond the fate of the seven Americans:

If Ebola crossed Kenya's borders tomorrow, is the country ready?

The answer, infectious disease experts say, lies not in panic but in years of quiet preparation that most Kenyans have never seen.

That preparedness became evident during a recent visit by The Standard to Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH), where access to one of the hospital's high-security isolation areas was restricted.

Hospital officials informed the reporting team that patients with Mpox were being managed in the unit and, for safety reasons, journalists were not allowed to enter or film inside.

The brief encounter offered a glimpse into the strict infection prevention measures that underpin Kenya's readiness for dangerous infectious diseases.

According to an infectious disease physician at the Kenyatta National Hospital and head of the isolation ward, preparedness is far more than having an isolation room.

"One thing we should never do as Kenyans is panic," he says. "Panic only makes the situation worse. Instead, we should ask ourselves one question: Are we prepared?"

His answer is unequivocal. "As a government and as health institutions, we are in preparedness mode."

Dr Nyukuri explains that preparedness begins long before the first patient arrives at a hospital.

It means evaluating whether enough trained personnel are available, whether laboratories have the necessary testing reagents, whether protective equipment is adequate, and whether health workers understand every step required to safely manage a suspected Ebola patient.

"Here at Kenyatta National Hospital, we have conducted extensive training for healthcare workers," he says. "We have carried out readiness assessments, simulated patient scenarios and practised every stage of care from the moment a suspected patient arrives, through admission, isolation and treatment."

The simulations, he explains, are designed to ensure that no decision is being made for the first time during a real emergency. "When we eventually encounter a suspected case, it should not be something new to us." Dr Duncan Nyukuri, an Infectious Diseases specialist, during an interview with The Standard on July 16, 2026 at Kenyatta National Hospital. [Benard Orwongo, Standard]

Preparedness also extends beyond hospitals. Health surveillance teams remain stationed at airports and land border crossings, screening travellers arriving from affected regions while rapid response teams stand ready to investigate suspected infections.

"So far, Kenya has done a good job," Dr Nyukuri says. "We have not recorded a confirmed case despite the increasing numbers in the DRC. We pray that remains the case. But if we receive one patient, we are prepared."

How Ebola jumps from animals to people

Although Ebola is often associated with outbreaks, the virus begins its journey quietly in nature.

Dr Nyukuri explains that fruit bats are believed to be the natural reservoir of the virus. "They carry the virus without becoming sick themselves," he says.

Problems arise when increasing human activity brings people into closer contact with wildlife.

Mining, logging, hunting, charcoal burning, expanding settlements and encroachment into forests all increase the likelihood of viruses crossing from animals into humans.

"We call these zoonotic diseases," Dr Nyukuri explains. "Once the virus infects a human being, it can then spread from person to person through contact with infected body fluids, leading to outbreaks within families and communities."

You see, Ebola is a family; many people speak about Ebola as though it were a single virus.

In reality, scientists recognise five different species.

The best known is the Zaire strain, responsible for the devastating West African epidemic between 2014 and 2016.

"It is highly infectious and highly deadly," says Dr Nyukuri. "But because we have studied it extensively, we now have licensed vaccines and effective treatment options."

The Sudan strain, which has repeatedly caused outbreaks in Uganda, is the second most significant.

The current emergency, however, involves the Bundibugyo strain, first identified in Uganda's Bundibugyo District.

"This is the third recorded outbreak caused by Bundibugyo," Dr Nyukuri explains. "We have not studied it nearly as much as the Zaire strain."

There is currently no licensed vaccine specifically targeting Bundibugyo Ebola.

Instead, researchers are evaluating experimental vaccines while clinical trials in eastern DRC are testing promising treatments, including the monoclonal antibody MBP134 and the antiviral drug remdesivir.

"That is why this outbreak concerns many of us," he says. "We still have limited tools compared to what exists for the Zaire strain."

While Kenya has not recorded a confirmed case linked to the current outbreak, neighbouring countries remain on high alert.

Uganda on Thursday declared its last Ebola patient and has begun the mandatory 42-day countdown required before the country can officially be declared Ebola-free.

In contrast, eastern DRC continues battling sustained transmission, placing enormous pressure on treatment centres and frontline health workers.

It is against that backdrop that Kenya has found itself playing an increasingly important role in regional preparedness.

Their presence has nevertheless fuelled public debate over Kenya's preparedness infrastructure and the country's place in global health security.

Earlier this week, two American humanitarian workers who contracted Ebola while working in eastern DRC were medically evacuated to Germany for specialised treatment after receiving initial care in Bunia. Their evacuation underscores an important distinction: Kenya is currently serving as a precautionary observation site for exposed but healthy personnel, while confirmed Ebola patients requiring advanced clinical care have been transferred to Germany.

For Dr Nyukuri, the conversation should remain grounded in science rather than fear.

Preparedness, he says, is not measured only by isolation wards or specialised equipment, but by the ability of an entire health system to detect threats early, respond quickly and protect both patients and healthcare workers.

"My prayer is that Kenya never records a case," he says. "But preparedness means planning for the day you hope never comes."

As seven healthy humanitarian workers quietly complete their quarantine in Kenya, that preparation is no longer an abstract exercise.

It is being tested in real time. The development has also drawn attention to the contrasting roles played by East African countries during the current outbreak.

Uganda, widely regarded as one of Africa's most experienced countries in responding to Ebola, recently brought its own outbreak under control and has now entered the 42-day countdown required to be declared Ebola-free. Over the years, the country has built a reputation for rapidly detecting cases, tracing contacts and isolating patients, earning praise from the World Health Organization for repeatedly containing outbreaks before they spread widely.

Yet despite that experience, Uganda did not become a destination for foreign humanitarian workers requiring precautionary quarantine or post-exposure observation.

Instead, that role has fallen to Kenya, where seven American aid workers are now completing a mandatory 21-day quarantine after working in Ebola-affected areas of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

The contrast raises broader questions about how countries are selected to support international outbreak responses. While Uganda has demonstrated its capacity to treat Ebola patients within its own borders, Kenya's involvement appears to reflect a different function—serving as a precautionary observation site for exposed personnel rather than a treatment centre for confirmed cases.

Health experts caution against interpreting the distinction as a measure of either country's clinical capability. Instead, they say such decisions are often influenced by a combination of bilateral agreements, operational logistics, evacuation arrangements and the specific objectives of international public health partners.

World.title: MPs push for urgent resolution of higher education funding crisis
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

HELB Chief Executive Officer Geoffrey Monari before the National Assembly Departmental Committee on Education on July 16, 2026. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

The National Assembly Departmental Committee on Education has called for urgent and coordinated action to address persistent funding challenges affecting Kenya's higher education sector.

The MPs proposed a joint engagement involving Parliament, the National Treasury and the Ministry of Education to streamline implementation of the Higher Education Funding Model.

The committee, chaired by Vice Chairperson Eve Obara, made the recommendation after holding separate meetings with officials from the State Department for Higher Education, the Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) and the Universities Fund during a review of the 2025/2026 Budget Implementation Status.

Appearing before the committee, Higher Education Principal Secretary Dr. Beatrice Inyangala said the Higher Education Funding Model is operational but continues to face implementation challenges due to inadequate alignment between the funding framework and budget allocations.

"The funding model is functional. However, the main challenge lies in budget alignment," Dr. Inyangala told Members.

The funding model was introduced to allocate financial support to university students based on their level of need, while ensuring sustainable financing for public universities.

However, implementation has generated debate over affordability, funding adequacy and delays in disbursement of resources to institutions.

MPs observed that the mismatch between policy and budgetary allocations has undermined effective financing of universities and agreed that a joint meeting involving the National Treasury, the Ministry of Education and Parliament would help harmonise the funding framework.

The committee also sought explanations over the growing stock of pending bills owed by public universities.

Dr. Inyangala informed Members that most of the outstanding obligations were inherited over several years, with universities continuing efforts to clear the debts despite increasing interest charges.

According to the State Department for Higher Education, public universities had accumulated pending bills amounting to Sh100.3 billion as of January 2026.

The ministry said institutions are prioritising settlement of pending obligations, suspending stalled development projects and exploring alternative revenue streams to prevent further accumulation of debt.

During a separate session, Members questioned HELB officials on how the board allocates student loans when available funding cannot meet demand from all eligible applicants.

Led by Chief Executive Officer Geoffrey Monari, HELB officials were asked to explain the criteria used in determining beneficiaries during periods of constrained resources.

Legislators emphasised that the allocation process should be fair, transparent and predictable to protect deserving students from being unfairly excluded.

World.title: “Not a single drop of oil”: Iran issues stark warning to US over infrastructure threats
World.content:
The Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters stated in a press release on Wednesday, that US President Donald Trump has resumed threatening Iran with strikes on its infrastructure.

“The Strait of Hormuz remains closed, and if any vessel is permitted passage, it will proceed solely along the designated route and under the previously announced protocols,” the headquarters’ leadership said in the statement.

The statement added that if the United States carries out its threats, the Iranian Armed Forces will not allow “even a single drop of oil to be exported,” warning that oil, gas, electricity, and economic infrastructure throughout the region will become targets for attacks.

It further stressed that repeated threats from the US and its military will only broaden the scope of the war across the region, and potentially beyond.

Trump had previously declared that “if Iran fires a missile, shell, drone, or any other weapon at a ship in the Strait of Hormuz at any time, the United States will bomb and destroy a bridge or power station—including those located in or near the capital, Tehran.

World.title: Reviving a legend: Farrah El Dibany to star in new musical bringing Dalida’s life story to the stage
World.content:
A new Egyptian-French musical play commemorating the 40th anniversary of the legendary singer Dalida’s passing, was officially announced during a press conference at the residence of the French Ambassador in Cairo. The launch featured French Ambassador Éric Chevallier, Egyptian mezzo-soprano Farrah El Dibany, film director Khairy Beshara, and writer Waleed Khairy.

The project is an Egyptian-French collaboration staged as part of the “Mediterranean Season 2026,” an initiative aimed at fostering cultural and artistic exchange among regional nations while highlighting the shared creativity and cultural diversity of Mediterranean peoples.

Scheduled to serve as the grand finale of the season, the production will premiere at the Bibliotheca Alexandrina on October 31, followed by performances in Cairo in November.

During the press conference, French Ambassador Éric Chevallier underscored the vital significance of Egyptian-French cultural cooperation, noting that the production represents a major step in reviving Dalida’s legacy through a joint musical theater venture.

For her part, Farrah El Dibany shared that portraying Dalida had been a childhood dream. She explained that she pitched the concept to director Khairy Beshara, who collaborated with writer Waleed Khairy to develop the idea into a full-fledged theatrical project.

Beshara stated that the work aims to present different facets of Dalida’s personality beyond her familiar stage persona, while writer Waleed Khairy explained that his script focuses on humanizing the artist by highlighting lesser-known aspects of her life. The production is produced by Ahmed Fawzi.

The play chronicles Dalida’s artistic and personal journey, emphasizing her deep connection to Egypt and the profound impact of her Egyptian upbringing on her artistic identity. It also features a fresh musical vision arranged by French-Armenian composer André Manoukian.

The show falls under the umbrella of the “Mediterranean Season 2026,” an initiative launched in 2023 by French President Emmanuel Macron and organized with the support of the French Ministries of Foreign Affairs and Culture.

Running from May 15 to October 31, 2026, across France and several Mediterranean nations—including Egypt, Lebanon, Tunisia, Algeria, and Morocco—the initiative seeks to strengthen cultural ties and support creative endeavors throughout the region.

World.title: Flight cancellations and airspace closures expected as US raises worldwide security alert
World.content:
The US Department of State has issued a security alert advising American citizens worldwide to exercise heightened caution amid escalating tensions in the Middle East and a increasingly complex security environment, warning of potential unexpected developments and further escalation.

The Department emphasized that US citizens currently in the Middle East should maintain a high state of vigilance and prepare for possible flight cancellations, temporary airspace closures, and travel disruptions. It noted that several airlines have postponed the resumption of previously scheduled flights, while others have canceled specific routes altogether.

Additionally, the State Department urged citizens outside the Middle East to reconsider traveling to or transiting through the region, advising travelers to continuously monitor the operational status of airports and airlines.

The advisory pointed out that US diplomatic facilities—including some located outside the Middle East—have been targeted, warning that Iran and its aligned proxy groups may target additional U.S. interests abroad or sites affiliated with the United States and American citizens globally, including commercial enterprises and other institutions.

World.title: When will the Barcelona vs. Al Ahly Joan Gamper Trophy match take place?
World.content:
The management of Spanish giants FC Barcelona has decided to face Egypt’s Al Ahly SC in a historic friendly match as part of the upcoming edition of the annual Joan Gamper Trophy.

According to a report published by the Spanish newspaper Mundo Deportivo, Al Ahly will be Barcelona’s opponent in the exhibition match. The report highlighted that Barcelona will take on a team boasting a massive fanbase across Egypt, Africa, and the Arab world. Additionally, Moroccan journalist Ashraf Ben Ayad, who is close to the Catalan club, confirmed that the Egyptian powerhouse will serve as Barcelona’s opponent in the upcoming edition of the tournament, which is held annually as a warm-up for the new season.

The highly anticipated fixture between Al Ahly and the Catalan club is scheduled for August 19, marking Barcelona’s season opener at the Camp Nou.

The match aligns with Barcelona’s strategy to strengthen ties with prominent Arab clubs while capitalizing on the Red Giants’ massive popularity and commercial pull throughout the Middle East.

World.title: Peak heatwave hits Egypt: EMA warns of worst 24 hours with soaring heat and humidity
World.content:
Egypt’s Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) has issued a weather update for Cairo and the governorates, warning that a severe heatwave across most parts of the country is reaching its peak.

Extremely hot and humid conditions are expected during the day in most regions, with hot and humid weather along the northern coast. Moderately warm and humid conditions will prevail overnight and into the early morning.

In its statement, the authority detailed that expected high temperatures will hit 40°C in Greater Cairo, reaching 43°C in Upper Egypt, 41°C in Northern Upper Egypt, 39°C in the Nile Delta, 35°C along the northwestern coast, and 33°C along the northeastern coast.

The EMA added that elevated humidity levels will intensify the feel-like temperature, driving the heat index up to 42°C in Greater Cairo, 44°C in Southern Upper Egypt, and 43°C in Northern Upper Egypt, marking what is expected to be the most intense 24-hour stretch of this heatwave.

Weather maps indicate the formation of morning fog between 4:00 AM and 8:00 AM across parts of northern Egypt extending to Greater Cairo, the Canal Cities, Central Sinai, and Northern Upper Egypt, which may be dense at times on select roadways.

The report also noted intermittent wind activity across most areas, offering slight evening relief in open spaces. However, active winds along parts of the Mediterranean coastline—including El Saloum, Matrouh, El Alamein, Alexandria, and Baltim—are expected to produce wave heights ranging between 1.5 and 2.25 meters.

Furthermore, the authority pointed to a minor chance of low-lying cloud formation over scattered areas of the northern coast, the Nile Delta, Greater Cairo, and the Canal Cities, which could lead to light, non-disruptive drizzle in isolated spots.

The EMA urged the public to avoid direct sunlight during peak hours and stay well-hydrated by drinking plenty of water and fluids, with a special emphasis on the elderly, children, individuals with chronic illness, and outdoor workers.

World.title: Prolonged blackouts and soaring heat leave several Egyptian governorates in darkness
World.content:
Several villages and towns across the governorates of Qalyubia, the Red Sea, Port Said, Sharqia, and Minya are experiencing a major crisis due to prolonged power outages lasting for hours at irregular intervals.

The blackouts, which occurred without prior warning to residents, have sparked widespread anger and resentment—particularly amid soaring temperatures, rising humidity, and the intense summer heat of July. Meanwhile, officials from electricity supply companies attributed the power instability during this period to extreme temperatures and increased strain on the grid.

Residents called for the immediate intervention of governors and members of parliament to swiftly contain the crisis and transparently announce its causes and mitigation plans. They emphasized that frequent electricity and water cuts have caused them significant financial losses, damaging numerous household appliances and repeatedly disrupting water pumping stations.

The recurring power cuts continued to impact a large number of neighborhoods, towns, and villages across the governorates.

Residents stated that the issue is no longer limited to “emergency breakdowns,” but has become an almost daily occurrence without official statements clarifying the reasons for the outages or estimated times for service restoration. This has heightened anxiety and disruption among families—especially those caring for the elderly, children, or patients who rely on stable living conditions and powered medical equipment.

They added that prolonged blackouts during peak hours turn their homes into unbearable heat traps, particularly given the high humidity.

The impact has also extended to the commercial sector; owners of grocery stores, supermarkets, restaurants, and cafes confirmed that repeated outages cause direct financial losses due to failing refrigerators and coolers, the risk of spoiled food items, and the disruption of electronic payment systems and internet service.

World.title: Egypt supports any pathway leading to a complete Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon
World.content:
Egyptian Ambassador to Lebanon Alaa Moussa reaffirmed Cairo’s steadfast support for any path leading to a complete Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory, emphasizing Egypt’s active efforts to end Israeli attacks and enable the Lebanese state to assert full control over its lands.

Moussa made the statements on Wednesday following a meeting with Lebanese Speaker of Parliament Nabih Berri at Ain El-Tineh. He noted that discussions focused on stopping Israeli assaults, empowering state authority, and assessing regional developments impacting Lebanon.

The ambassador stated that he briefed Berri on “the latest developments and Cairo’s ongoing efforts to de-escalate tensions and facilitate a return to the negotiating table regarding the situation between the United States and Iran.”

He added that Speaker Berri reiterated several critical priorities, namely “an immediate and complete halt to Israeli attacks on Lebanon, full withdrawal from all Lebanese territories, the return of displaced persons, and the launch of reconstruction efforts.”

“Egypt’s position remains firm and unambiguous: we support any pathway that ultimately leads to a full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon, the return of our displaced brothers and sisters to their towns and villages, and the commencement of rebuilding under a clear timetable,” Moussa said, underscoring Cairo’s full backing for initiatives aimed at achieving these goals.

Highlighting recent progress, the ambassador pointed out that operations began in designated “pilot zones” the previous day. He expressed hope that this step would expand to other areas to pave the way for a complete Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese soil, stressing that success hinges on the commitment of all parties and providing the necessary support and resources to the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF).

Moussa further emphasized the importance of empowering the Lebanese army to fulfill its mandate, stating that Egypt supports hosting an international conference to back the LAF. He noted that Cairo had hosted a preparatory conference for this purpose earlier this year and expressed optimism that remaining obstacles to holding the main conference would be resolved.

He concluded by noting that he updated the Lebanese Parliament Speaker on Cairo’s latest diplomatic moves to defuse regional tensions, including efforts aimed at reviving negotiations between Washington and Tehran.

World.title: Huthi blockade threat raises risk of dual energy chokepoint crisis, Kpler says
World.content:
A threat by the Iranian backed Houthis to blockade Saudi-linked shipping in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait has raised the prospect of the Middle East’s two key energy chokepoints coming under pressure at the same time, shipping analytics firm Kpler warned Tuesday.

A “simultaneous and prolonged disruption of Bab el-Mandeb and the Strait of Hormuz could affect maritime routes carrying approximately one-quarter of global oil supply,” the firm said in a written analysis.

The firm said Bab el-Mandeb – which connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean – remains open, but traffic is already running far below pre-crisis levels while conditions in Hormuz have “deteriorated sharply.”

According to Kpler, crossings through Bab el-Mandeb averaged about 41 vessels a day between July 15 and July 20, “43% below the 2023 peak of 72/day.”

Saudi crude loadings through the strait fell 34% in two weeks, dropping from 29.58 million barrels in the week of June 29 to 19.50 million barrels in the week of July 13, the analysis said.

Kpler said the Houthi threat is especially significant because Saudi Arabia has increasingly used the Red Sea route as a fallback for exports after disruption in the Strait of Hormuz.

Kpler examined several possible scenarios, ranging from limited self-diversion by cautious operators to a full blockade. Under “selective targeting,” it said, “compliant commercial traffic could fall 40–50% within weeks, pushing crossings toward 20–25/day.” Under a full blockade, Bab el-Mandeb “could follow Hormuz and fall below 15 vessels/day within days,” the analysis said.

In a separate note published Tuesday, Kpler said two tankers carrying Saudi crude reversed course in the Red Sea after the Houthi declaration.

World.title: VP Nalumango outlines UPND campaign promises to Chifunabuli
World.content:
Vice President Mutale Nalumango has laid out a series of campaign promises to the people of Chifunabuli District, urging them to re-elect the United Party for National Development (UPND) on 13th August to ensure these commitments are fulfilled.

Mrs Nalumango promised that the free education policy would continue, citing its impact so far in the district.

“Your royal highnesses, the free education policy here in Chifunabuli District has since its introduction for instance brought 400 pupils back to school,” she said.

She further backed this promise with data from Chifunabuli District Education Standards Officer, Grace Kambobe, who reported that learner enrolment has surged from 26,522 in 2021 to 41,732 currently, with 403 teachers recruited and many schools benefiting from the school feeding programme and the Keeping Girls in School initiative.

The Vice President promised that the construction of the Musaila – Lubwe – Kasaba Road to bituminous standard is already underway, with contractors on site — a project she said the UPND had responded to after calls from the community.

Mrs Nalumango promised the continuation of various developmental programmes across the country, including the enhanced Constituency Development Fund (CDF), as acknowledged by the Chifunabuli Pastors Fellowship.

Addressing civil servants, she promised that effective delivery of development would be achieved if public servants work as a unified unit with the government and remain in sync with government policy to guarantee smooth implementation of programmes.

The Vice President also promised to push for national production targets, encouraging civil servants to take up farming to boost food security and income, citing the government’s goal to increase maize output to 10 million tonnes and soya beans to three million tonnes.

She further promised continued support for education infrastructure, with Lubwe Secondary Boarding School Headteacher, Misheck Chirwa, thanking the government through the Vice President for a fully-fledged boarding secondary school already delivered in Mwewa chiefdom.

Mrs Nalumango stated that continuity of all these developmental projects hinges on the electorate turning out to re-elect the UPND on 13th August.

Traditional leaders, including Chief Chitembo, have already hailed the government for the free education policy and the roadworks, while the Pastors Fellowship, through Chairperson Dominic Mubanga, said the clergy stands ready as partners in development and would remain steadfast in prayer for government as they continue to administer critical development across the country.

World.title: Solwezi woman dies due to phone battery explosion
World.content:
A 23- year- old woman of Ikelenge District of North-Western Province has died after she was struck on the neck by a cellphone battery that exploded as a result of the fire.

North-Western Province Commissioner of Police, Brighton Mwale, confirmed the incident in a statement issued in Solwezi yesterday and identified the victim as Jean Ntambu aged 22 of Matoka village.

He said the matter was reported on July 22, 2026 by the victim’s brother, Guard Ntambu, aged 26, that his young sister, Jean Ntambu, aged 23, of the same abode, died after she was struck by a cell phone battery that exploded on the fire and caused her to sustain a deep cut on her neck at about 18:00 hours at Matoka village.

Mr Siwale said brief facts of the matter are that on 22nd July, 2026 at about 17:00 hours the deceased was cleaning the surrounding and hipped the dirty at one point and set it on fire.

He explained that while burning the dirt, the deceased sat near the fire without realising that amongst the dirt was a dead cell phone battery which exploded and some particles hit her on her neck causing her to sustain a deep cut and heavy bleeding.

Mr Siwale said the victim was rushed to a rural health post where she was attended to and later transferred to Kalene Mission Hospital where she was pronounced dead upon arrival.

“Acting on the report police rushed to Ikelenge Rural Health Post where the victim was rushed to and found the health personnel attending to the victim, and the condition was critical. A deep cut on the neck and severe bleeding was observed,” Mr Siwale said.

He said the body of the deceased has since been deposited in Kalene Mission Hospital mortuary awaiting postmortem examination and burial.

Mr Siwale has warned members of the public to be mindful in the manner and way they dispose of gadgets waste to avoid similar unfortunate circumstances in their communities in the future.

World.title: 8 Not 7: ECZ’s Unopposed Seat Count Falls Short, and Lumezi North Goes Unexplained
World.content:
Eight, Not Seven: ECZ’s Unopposed Seat Count Falls Short, and Lumezi North Goes Unexplained

Lusaka. A review of the Electoral Commission of Zambia’s (ECZ) own nomination records has turned up two discrepancies ahead of the 13 August general election. One is an undercount in the number of uncontested National Assembly seats. The other is the unexplained disappearance of an entire constituency from the Commission’s official candidate list.

In a public announcement this month, ECZ told stakeholders that, apart from the presidential race, several candidates had been declared unopposed across the mayoral, National Assembly, and local government by-elections. The Commission recorded six unopposed mayoral candidates out of 116 districts, seven unopposed National Assembly candidates out of 226 constituencies, and 176 unopposed candidates for local government out of 1,858 wards.

A check of ECZ’s own Notice of Validly Nominated Candidates for the 2026 Parliamentary Elections, dated 22 July 2026, tells a different story. Eight constituencies carry only one validly nominated candidate each, not seven. All eight went to the United Party for National Development (UPND): Keembe West in Central Province, Zambezi West and Liuwa in the west, and five constituencies clustered in Southern Province, namely Choma South, Dundumwezi, Kalomo South, Kazungula North, and Sinazongwe.

The gap is one seat. But it sits inside a document that candidates, party agents, and voters are meant to treat as authoritative. ECZ has not publicly clarified which figure is correct.

A separate and more serious gap concerns Lumezi North constituency in Eastern Province’s Lumezi District. The constituency does not appear anywhere in the 22 July nomination notice. It is missing from the contested seats, missing from the unopposed seats, and missing without a single explanatory note.

The reason traces back to a death. Three candidates had lodged nominations for Lumezi North in May: Anderson Banda of the ruling UPND, Nebby Manda of the Leadership Movement, and Clement Mwale, standing for the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) under the Tonse Pamodzi Alliance banner. Mwale had served as Lumezi Council Chairperson between 2016 and 2021. He died in the early hours of 16 July 2026. Tonse Pamodzi Alliance’s Eastern Province chairperson, Maxson Nkhoma, confirmed the death in a statement.

Zambian election law changed significantly in 2025. Under Constitutional Amendment No. 13 of that year, a candidate who resigns or is disqualified by a court after nominations close no longer forces the Commission to cancel that election. The reform was designed to stop late withdrawals from disrupting the vote. Death, however, was kept as a distinct exception. Article 52(6)(c) of the Constitution still requires ECZ to cancel the poll for that constituency and give the candidate’s sponsoring party thirty days to nominate a replacement. ECZ’s own nomination guidance sets out the same rule. ECZ Commissioner McDonald Chipenzi, briefing reporters in Dubai on ballot paper printing, confirmed that this obligation applies to Lumezi North following Mwale’s death.

The legal process is not in question. What is missing is any acknowledgement of it in the document meant to inform the public. Anyone working from the 22 July notice alone, a resident of Lumezi North, a journalist, a party agent, would have no way of knowing why their constituency is not there. It could just as easily read as a printing fault, a missed submission, or an unresolved dispute. The notice does not say otherwise.

Neither issue is, on its own, a major scandal. An undercount of one seat is an administrative slip. A constituency’s absence, once explained, turns out to rest on a lawful and defensible basis. That is precisely the point. These are small, answerable questions, and ECZ has not answered them.

Zambian elections run across 226 constituencies, 116 districts, and 1,858 wards, at enormous cost and under real time pressure. Nobody disputes that ECZ is stretched thin. But a national election depends on public confidence in the paperwork as much as in the polling itself. That confidence is built one clarified query at a time. It is not damaged by any single unanswered question so much as by a habit of treating small questions from the public as beneath a response. A one-line note explaining Lumezi North, or a corrected figure in the unopposed count, would have cost the Commission almost nothing and closed both matters before they became a story.

ECZ should treat no query as too small, no discrepancy as too minor, and no member of the public raising one as a nuisance. That habit of responsiveness, more than any single correction, is what keeps an electoral process credible in the eyes of the people it serves.

This publication has sought clarification from ECZ on both the correct number of uncontested National Assembly seats and the current status of the Lumezi North re-nomination process. This story will be updated with the Commission’s response.

source: ECZ’s Notice of Validly Nominated Candidates for the 2026 Parliamentary Elections (22 July 2026), ECZ’s public announcement on unopposed candidates, ECZ’s published nominations guidance, Constitutional Amendment No. 13 of 2025,

World.title: Govt. to modernize agric extension services
World.content:
Government has reaffirmed its commitment to modernising agricultural extension services through digital innovation with the rollout of the Mulimi360 e-extension Platform.

Ministry of Agriculture Permanent Secretary for Technical Services John Mulogoti says the initiative is aimed at improving access to timely and reliable information for farmers across the country.

Speaking during the provincial rollout and sensitisation meeting on the Mulimi360 e-Extension Platform held at Urban Hotel in Kasama yesterday, Mr Mulongoti says the initiative marks a significant milestone in strengthening and modernising agricultural extension service delivery.

Mr Mulongoti said the platform demonstrates the government’s commitment to embracing innovation and digital transformation to enhance climate resilience, food and nutrition security, job creation and sustainable socio-economic growth.

He said the development of the platform was made possible through the support of cooperating partners, including the European Union, which financed the Sustainable Intensification of Smallholder Farming Systems in Zambia project.

“The development of Mulimi360 demonstrates the power of partnership in advancing national development priorities,” he said.

He noted that government policy through the Comprehensive Agricultural Transformation Support Programme (CATSP) and the Eighth National Development Plan (8NDP) priorities increased agricultural production and productivity by creating an enabling environment that attracts private sector investment.

Mr Mulongoti said the interventions are already bearing fruit with Zambia projected to record a bumper maize harvest of more than five million metric tonnes during the current farming season.

He further disclosed that President Hakainde Hichilema has tasked the Ministry of Agriculture with achieving annual production targets of 10 million metric tonnes of maize, three million metric tonnes of soyabeans, one million metric tonnes of wheat and one million metric tonnes of sugar by 2031.

“The Ministry stands ready to actualise these targets through close collaboration with all stakeholders, leveraging innovation, digital transformation and private sector participation,” he said.

Mr Mulongoti emphasised that digital technologies have become a strategic necessity in improving service delivery and strengthening climate resilience, adding that conventional extension services alone are no longer sufficient to meet the growing needs of farmers.

He explained that the Mulimi360 Platform consists of a web portal, mobile application and the e-Mulangizi chatbot, which together provide integrated agricultural advisory services, early warning and climate information, market intelligence, geospatial data management and digital knowledge repositories.

He said the platform will enable farmers to access timely, accurate and reliable information to support informed decision-making and improve agricultural productivity.

Mr Mulongoti urged the Ministry of Agriculture staff at all levels to take ownership of the platform and ensure that accurate and quality information is consistently uploaded to maximise its effectiveness.

He further called on all departments within the Ministry to work together in supporting the integrated digital platform, describing agricultural development as a multidisciplinary undertaking that requires collaboration.

Mr Mulongoti expressed confidence that the successful implementation of Mulimi360 will contribute significantly to increased agricultural productivity, climate resilience, food security and sustainable agriculture.

Meanwhile, Northern Province Agricultural Coordinator Aswel Lubungo observed that agricultural extension services remain an essential link between research, policy, markets and farmers.

Mr Lubungo said the provision of electronic extension services presents an opportunity to make agricultural information easily accessible, relevant and timely for farmers across the province.

He noted that the development of the Mulimi360 platform marks a significant step towards improving communication among farmers, agricultural extension officers and the Ministry of Agriculture.

“The development of the Mulimi360 platform is a significant development towards improving communication among farmers, agricultural extension officers and the Ministry at large,” Mr, Lubungo said.

And National Project Coordinator for Mulimi360 e-Extension platform, Geoffrey Siulembe said the project is intended to improve agricultural productivity by strengthening access to agricultural extension services and information.

Dr Siulembe said the digital platform will ensure that farmers receive accurate and timely information to support informed decision making and enhance production.

And one of the participants, Kisha Mulenga welcomed the initiative, describing it as a timely intervention that will benefit farmers.

Ms Mulenga said the project will enable farmers to easily access information on agriculture including best farming practices and other extension services.

She added that improved access to agricultural information will help farmers increase productivity in various districts and contribute to agricultural development in Northern Province.

The Mulimi360 e-Extension Platform is expected to strengthen communication between farmers and extension officers while enhancing the delivery of agricultural advisory services through the use of digital technology.

World.title: Govt. to construct modern hospital in Chirundu – President Hichilema
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has announced that government will construct an ultra-modern district hospital with matching state of the art equipment in Chirundu District of Southern Province.

President Hichilema has further assured that the government will complete the Lusitu irrigation project to enhance agriculture productivity.

Addressing thousands of Chirundu residents during a community engagement at Boom ground, Mr Hichilema urged the people to vote for the ruling United Party for National Development (UPND) in the August 13 General Elections for continued peace, sustained social protection programmes and wider development.

“Vote for peace, free education, and expansion of Social Cash Transfer (SCT) to allow for the initiation of more beneficiaries and wider development.

“We will construct an ultra-modern district hospital with matching state of the art equipment and employ qualified health personnel,” Mr Hichilema said.

He stated that once re-elected on August 13, government will build houses for civil servants in Chirundu and upgrade township roads to bituminous standards.

The Head of State also directed for the recruitment of all volunteer health workers in the district and urged for calm among other prospective employees, stating that their turn is coming.

He added that his administration will also prioritise the rebuilding of the Chirundu border to improve the movement of goods and create more jobs, once re-elected.

Mr Hichilema also observed that the kwacha is the best performing currency among other convertible currencies and advised the people of Chirundu to vote for him and all UPND adopted candidates to maintain the momentum.

President Hichilema said the UPND must win big in the forthcoming polls and urged people not to split votes but vote for the ruling party.

“The president requires a dedicated team in order to deliver. Therefore, vote suit for UPND for continued effective service delivery. Don’t waste your vote on opposition or independent candidates. Voting for opposition or independent would be ominous,” he underscored.

And UPND Alliance partner and PF President, Miles Sampa, has condemned a named opposition party for using the late former President Edgar Lungu as a campaign tool.

“I’m shocked that some opposition party yesterday had the audacity to put the former late President Edgar Lungu on display in a campaign move. This is un-Zambian and must be condemned,” Mr Sampa said.

World.title: Over 1, 000 Mbala farmers to benefit from input distribution
World.content:
Over 1000 Farmers are expected to benefit from the distribution of farming inputs under the Wetlands Farming Programme in Mbala District of Northern province.

Mbala District Community Development Officer, Theresa Nsakashalo, has disclosed that some of the farming inputs under the programme have since been delivered.

Ms Nsakashalo has told the media in an interview that so far government has delivered 1,050 50-kilogram bags of D-Compound fertiliser and 1,050 5-kilogram packs of white maize seed.

She revealed that the department has received all of its allocated D-Compound fertiliser and white maize seed for distribution to beneficiaries.

Ms Nsakashalo indicated that the remaining inputs yet to be received are 1,050 50-kilogram bags of urea top-dressing fertiliser and 1,050 25-kilogram bags of agricultural lime, which will complete the allocation under the Wetlands Farming Programme.

“Government is on course to ensure all farming inputs are delivered on time, and I can reveal that all the allocated D- Compound Fertiliser, and Maize seed have been delivered.

“1,050 beneficiaries are expected to benefit from the programme, and hope that this will not just improve food security in communities but also livelihoods of the people,” she added.

Ms Nsakashalo noted that the timely delivery of farming inputs will help improve agricultural productivity and strengthen household food security in the district.

Government has been implementing the Wetlands Farming Programme aimed at ensuring household food security across the country.

World.title: Mufulira District Administration Offices to have solar-powered borehole
World.content:
Government has commenced the installation of a solar-powered borehole valued at K300,000 at Mufulira District Administration Offices to address chronic water challenges that have severely compromised sanitation at the premises.

Mufulira District Commissioner, Evaristo Chilumba, revealed that the project is being implemented using the disaster component of the Constituency Development Fund (CDF).

Mr Chilumba stated that drilling of the borehole has already been completed, adding that pipe works, installation of the tank and solar panels are expected to be completed within one week.

He stated that the sanitation situation at the premises was an impending sanitary crisis, with a risk of an outbreak of waterborne diseases such as Cholera during the rainy season.

“The premises provide services to large numbers of people daily through national registration offices, the Ministry of Agriculture, the local and magistrate courts, and other government departments,” he said.

Mr Chilumba explained that the long standing water shortage left both visiting members of the public and staff with extremely limited sanitation services.

He further announced that government will also renovate the ablution block that was previously closed due to lack of water and subsequently converted into makeshift storerooms.

Department of Agriculture Senior Agricultural Officer, Belinda Sichamba, noted that officers and clients seeking services from the various government departments had long endured poor sanitation due to the lack of water.

“The installation of the borehole is going to improve the working conditions for the civil servants based at the district administration offices.

“As the Ministry of Agriculture, we service a lot of farmers, the National Registration Department as well as the Cooperatives Department also service a lot of community members who all need to use rooms of convenience,” she added.

Ms Sichamba has since noted that the installation of the borehole will enhance service delivery to the public.

World.title: Africa: Cotton to Cloth - The Story Africa Has Always Needed to Tell
World.content:
editorial

Africa grows more than half of the world's finest long-staple cotton. It earns less than three percent of what that cotton is eventually worth. This is not a trade problem. It is a narrative problem — and allAfrica is setting out to fix it.

There is a number that explains much of what is wrong with how the world finances Africa. It is not a trade figure or a debt ratio. It is an annual cost — up to $4.2 billion — the amount by which negative media stereotypes inflate African sovereign borrowing costs every single year. The story the world reads about Africa costs Africa, concretely, in higher interest rates and slower capital flows.

allAfrica has spent close to 3 decades building the infrastructure to change that story. Eight million articles in archive. A network of 140+ media partners spanning every corner of the continent. Direct distribution reaching tens of millions of decision-makers globally through Bloomberg, Dow Jones/Factiva, Thomson Reuters, Moody's Analytics/NewsEdge, LexisNexis, Syndigate & Tagaday (Europe). We are, in the most literal sense, the channel through which Africa's story reaches the people who price African risk.

Cotton to Cloth is the moment we unlock the full power of the infrastructure we have built over the years.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"The gap between raw commodity and finished product is not a production gap. It is a perception gap — and journalism, data, and storytelling can close it." — Amadou Mahtar Ba · Co-Founder, allAfrica Global Media

The initiative

Beginning June 2026 and running through December, allAfrica launches its most sustained and investment-grade editorial programme to date — a dedicated hub on all its platforms covering every dimension of Africa's cotton-to-cloth transformation, built on the conviction that Africa's cotton story — told well, distributed broadly, and anchored in data — can measurably shift how the world's capital allocators think about the continent.

The story begins in the field. West African cotton is among the finest on earth — long-staple, clean, commanding a premium on international markets. It leaves the continent as raw fibre. It returns as finished garments at twenty, thirty, sometimes fifty times the price. The countries that grow the raw material that clothes the world are rarely named as manufacturers. That is the gap this initiative addresses, one story at a time.

What you will find on this hub



This page is the entry point for all allAfrica content on this initiative. Over the coming months, it will grow into the most comprehensive English and French editorial resource on African cotton industrialisation available anywhere online — spanning original journalism, investor intelligence, documentary storytelling, policy analysis, and voices from across the continent and its diaspora.

Original long-form journalism. A sustained monthly publication series going deep on the economics, the geography, the people, and the policy architecture of Africa's cotton transformation — written to the standard that institutional investors, policymakers, and informed readers require. Evidence-based, rigorous, told from the inside.

Investor-grade data and intelligence. A major annual data publication mapping Africa's cotton processing investment landscape, a live deal tracker updated monthly, and sector intelligence briefs — all structured for capital markets audiences and distributed through allAfrica's global institutional wire network.

Policy voices and thought leadership. Commissioned essays, opinion pieces, and in-depth interviews bringing African ministers, industrialists, economists, and sector leaders directly to the audiences that shape policy and move capital — wire-distributed to the financial press and reaching Bloomberg, Factiva, LexisNexis, and beyond.

Documentary and multimedia storytelling. Original documentary features, a podcast series, and data-driven visual content placing human faces and real places at the centre of the industrial story — from the floor of a processing zone to the hands of a cooperative farmer, the cotton-to-cloth story in full depth and colour.

Close 

Youth and diaspora voices. A continent-wide storytelling contest inviting contributors from across Africa and the African diaspora to tell the cotton-to-cloth story in their own words. The next generation of African economic narrators, brought in from the first day.

Live events and convenings. A virtual roundtable, a physical exhibition at the allAfrica Media Leaders Summit, and allAfrica's presence at major African institutional forums throughout the year — taking this story from screen to room.

Follow the story



Everything on this hub is free. Every article, data release, documentary, and podcast will be published in both English and French — because the cotton-to-cloth story is as much a Francophone African story as it is an Anglophone one, and allAfrica serves the full continent.
